title: BUG: silent zero-vector fallback in gateway embedding service ships degenerate embeddings
description:
Discovered during Tier-2 memory architect analysis. sera-gateway/src/services/embedding.rs:153 and :161 return vec![0.0; 384] on any Ollama error. This silently ships degenerate embeddings for every memory_search and semantic-recall call — zero-vector cosine similarity is undefined/bogus, so any consumer gets garbage ranking without any log or metric to signal the failure.

Per SPEC-memory §13.3 and §13.6, embedding providers must fail loudly with the EmbeddingError::Provider taxonomy, not degrade silently.

Fix: delete both fallbacks; callers must handle Err path or bubble up. In the immediate term this is covered by sera-tier2-a (sera-czpa). If that bead slips, file this as a P0 hotfix.

Known callers: sera-gateway routes/embedding.rs + routes/memory.rs. No sera-runtime caller today, so blast radius is confined to gateway-side /api/embedding and /api/memory routes.

title: P0: schedule-task skill bypasses ScheduleService — schedules never fire
description: The schedule-task builtin skill (core/src/skills/builtins/schedule-task.ts) writes directly to the schedules table via raw SQL for ALL operations (create at line 212, activate at line 255, update at line 347, deactivate, delete). It never calls ScheduleService methods, so pg-boss cron jobs are never registered. Result: any schedule an agent creates or activates via the tool will NEVER FIRE until the next server restart triggers reconcile(). This blocks Sera inner life activation and all agent self-scheduling. Fix: replace all raw SQL with ScheduleService.getInstance() method calls.

title: implement P0 Docker-native security negative validation suite
description:
Parent strategy: `/home/entity/.hermes/ops/sera-docker-native-validation-strategy-2026-05-07.md`.

Implement the P0 Docker-native/security negative suite.

Cases:
- unauthenticated request to protected endpoint returns 401/403 and no token reflection.
- malformed bearer token returns 401/403 and no token reflection.
- capability-denied tool request fails closed where API surface exists; otherwise process/e2e test plus explicit API gap.
- missing policy reference fails closed.
- SSRF/tool request to loopback, RFC1918, metadata IP, link-local, and IPv6 private/loopback is blocked where HTTP/file tools are exposed.
- raw upstream/provider error is sanitized.
- empty assistant message with neither content nor tool calls does not leak raw provider error.
- operator false-green/interrupted runtime result remains a hard validation failure.

Acceptance:
- Every case has stable `case_id`, category, attack, expected signal, actual signal, pass/fail, and evidence fields.
- Any secret leak fails the whole profile.
- Any raw provider/internal path/token leak fails the whole profile.
- Denied action includes audit/evidence id when available; if audit is not wired, artifact records `audit_gap=true` rather than silently passing.
- Profile supports live-safe cases and ephemeral-compose-only destructive cases.
acceptance_criteria: P0 negative cases cover auth denial/token reflection, capability/missing policy fail-closed, SSRF blocked targets, raw provider error sanitization, empty assistant message handling, and false-green regression; artifacts include case ids, expected/actual/evidence, audit gap marker, and fail on any secret/internal leak.

title: docker-native validation harness for SERA security, performance, and accuracy
description:
Strategy artifact: `/home/entity/.hermes/ops/sera-docker-native-validation-strategy-2026-05-07.md`.

Context:
Sebastian explicitly directed that SERA development needs a Docker-native test strategy executable through subagents/profiles, covering performance, accuracy, negative tests, and security validation.

Why this matters:
SERA runs as a containerized product. Unit/in-process tests are necessary but insufficient. The validation layer must test the actual boundary: Docker compose service, container/network/secrets behavior, host model provider path, gateway/runtime/subagent path, operator card semantics, and negative/security failure modes.

Scope:
Create a Docker-native validation program that can run live smoke, security negative tests, Docker egress/boundary tests, performance/reliability baselines, accuracy/correctness suites, and feed findings back into beads/Kanban.

Key invariants:
- Negative tests are first-class.
- Security artifacts preserve evidence and redact secrets.
- HTTP 200 is not success unless semantic assertions pass.
- False-green results create failures, not passes.
- Harness supports both live stack (`rust-sera-1`) and ephemeral compose projects.
- Hermes Kanban/profiles are the cockpit; beads remain canonical.

Initial child sequence:
1. Harness skeleton / `sera-validate` CLI.
2. Security negative P0 suite.
3. Docker security overlay + egress expansion.
4. Performance/reliability baseline.
5. Accuracy output correctness suite.
6. Control-loop integration.
acceptance_criteria: Docker-native validation program exists with live and ephemeral compose modes; security negative tests, performance/reliability baselines, accuracy correctness tasks, egress/boundary checks, redacted artifacts, and loop feedback into beads/Kanban are implemented; false greens and secret/raw-provider leaks fail validation.

title: [bug] sera-gateway/discord: no RESUME — every reconnect re-IDENTIFIEs, dropping events between disconnect and reconnect
description: rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/discord.rs never extracts session_id or resume_gateway_url from the READY dispatch (handle_payload at line 358 only stores user_id/username), and connect_and_run always re-IDENTIFIEs on every reconnect (line 277). The Discord Gateway protocol requires storing session_id from READY and the highest seq the client has seen, then sending op 6 (RESUME) on a reconnect to receive missed dispatches. Without RESUME, every reconnect (network blip, op 7, op 9 with d:true, scheduled gateway close) drops events between the close and the next IDENTIFY, and counts toward the daily IDENTIFY budget. This is the primary message-loss path for the Discord agent surface.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Store session_id and resume_gateway_url from READY in DiscordConnector state. 2) Sequence already tracked via AtomicI64 — promote to be visible to outer reconnect loop. 3) New build_resume_payload(token, session_id, seq) helper with unit test. 4) connect_and_run: when a previous session exists, dial resume_gateway_url and send op 6 RESUME instead of op 2 IDENTIFY. 5) Integration-style test using a tokio_tungstenite mock server verifies RESUME on reconnect after a clean disconnect.
close_reason: Already completed in merged PR #1116 (39f92252/8ecbf6bf): Discord READY session_id/resume_gateway_url are stored, sequence survives reconnects, build_resume_payload exists, and reconnect path sends OP 6 RESUME when session state is cached.

title: [bug] sera-gateway/discord: Op 9 INVALID_SESSION not handled — bot can hot-loop INVALID_SESSION → IDENTIFY → INVALID_SESSION
description: Discord Gateway opcode 9 (INVALID_SESSION) is the canary that the current session can't be resumed. The d field is a boolean: when true the client should RESUME, when false it must wait 1-5s and IDENTIFY fresh. The current handle_payload in rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/discord.rs:354-399 has no arm for op 9 — it logs 'Unhandled opcode' and ignores the payload. With no session_id stored from READY (RESUME also missing), an op 9 closes the socket and the outer reconnect loop re-IDENTIFIEs immediately; if the upstream cause persists (token rotation, intent change, malformed identify) the bot hot-loops and burns the IDENTIFY budget.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Add OP_INVALID_SESSION (=9) handling that reads d:bool and either schedules a RESUME (when true) or a 1-5s jittered wait + fresh IDENTIFY (when false). 2) Unit test feeds {op:9, d:false} and asserts a wait-then-identify path; another with {op:9, d:true} asserts a resume-attempt path. 3) Wire to outer loop so the 5s fixed sleep is bypassed for op 9 (current sleep is unconditional).
close_reason: Already completed in merged PR #1116 (39f92252/8ecbf6bf): OP 9 INVALID_SESSION is handled with resume/fresh-identify behavior and regression coverage.

title: [bug] [security-availability] sera-gateway/discord: Op 7 RECONNECT not handled — falls through to 'Unhandled opcode' debug log
description: Discord Gateway opcode 7 (RECONNECT) instructs the bot to disconnect, RESUME on a new socket, and replay missed events. The current handle_payload match in rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/discord.rs:354-399 only handles OP_DISPATCH(0) and 11 (HEARTBEAT_ACK); op 7 hits the catch-all _ branch and is silently logged at debug. The connection stays open until Discord closes it, after which connect_and_run sleeps a fixed 5s and re-IDENTIFIEs. Real impact: in-flight events between Discord's RECONNECT signal and the eventual close are dropped, and every forced reconnect costs an IDENTIFY rate-limit slot (Discord caps these per 24h).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Add OP_RECONNECT (=7) constant. 2) handle_payload triggers a controlled close that exits the read loop. 3) Outer loop reconnects without re-IDENTIFY when session_id+sequence are tracked (paired with RESUME work, see related bead). 4) Unit test parses {op:7} and asserts the connector signals reconnect rather than ignoring it.
close_reason: Already completed in merged PR #1116 (39f92252/8ecbf6bf): OP 7 RECONNECT is handled as controlled reconnect/resume instead of falling through to unhandled-op logging.

title: [sera-3l84.4] Purge 97 tier: references — realize local/enterprise distinction through config only

title: [sera-3l84.2 — pivoted] Delete orphan Postgres routes/ + services/ tree; port unique features inline into bin/sera.rs

## New scope

title: [sera-3l84.1] Wire routes/state/services modules + introduce DbBackend trait abstraction
description:
First sub-bead of the sera-3l84 canonicalization epic.

## Scope
1. Declare mod routes; mod state; mod services; in rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/lib.rs so the 21K lines of code compile as part of the public library (not just --all-targets).
2. Introduce a DbBackend trait in rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/db_backend.rs (new file) that abstracts the operations state.rs::AppState currently does against sqlx::PgPool.
3. Provide two impls: PgPoolBackend (wraps sqlx::PgPool) and SqliteDbBackend (wraps bin/sera.rs's SqliteDb). Choose which via manifest config.
4. Update state.rs::AppState to hold Arc<dyn DbBackend> instead of sqlx::PgPool directly.
5. Do NOT touch bin/sera.rs yet — its inline handlers keep working against their own local AppState. This phase is the foundation only.

## Success criteria

- Porting bin handlers into routes/ — that's 3l84.2.
- Deleting bin handlers — that's 3l84.3.
- Purging 'tier:' references — that's 3l84.4.

Priority: P1. Parent: sera-3l84.

title: [architecture decision] Adopt or delete orphan src/routes/ + src/state.rs + src/services/ tree in sera-gateway (P1 — blocks 6+ follow-ups)
description:
Root cause identified by duplicate-implementation audit 2026-04-23.

## The fracture
An early Postgres/sqlx-based LIBRARY design exists under rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/routes/ (40+ files), rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/state.rs, and rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/services/ (28+ files). Neither src/lib.rs nor src/bin/sera.rs declares 'mod routes; mod state; mod services;'. The modules compile (cargo picks them up in --all-targets) but are NEVER bound to the production axum router.

Meanwhile, the MVS rewrite in src/bin/sera.rs authored its own inline handlers, its own AppState, its own ChatRequest/ChatResponse types, all against SqliteDb (not sqlx/Postgres). The binary builds its router at L3039-3077 using only bin-local handlers + a handful of route_a2a/route_agui/route_plugins crate-level exports.

## Evidence
- Verified via sera-local: /api/chat works (bin's handler); /api/agents/:id/tasks, /api/intercom/publish, /api/intercom/dm, /api/permission-requests all return 404 (routes/ not bound).
- sera-r1g8 (merged 2026-04-22) added envelope emission to the orphan routes — unreachable in production.
- bin/sera.rs:3083 has a comment that acknowledges the split: 'they currently depend on the Postgres-backed crate::state::AppState and crate::error::AppError from the library, incompatible with this binary's SqliteDb-backed AppState'.
- 11 concrete duplicates identified across chat types, AppState, UsageInfo, Submission, QueueBackend, TranscriptEntry, session persistence (see audit report in session notes).

## The decision (pick one — both require substantial work)

**Option A — Adopt the routes/ tree as canonical.**
- Declare 'mod routes; mod state; mod services;' in lib.rs + bin/sera.rs.
- Migrate src/state.rs::AppState from sqlx::PgPool to whatever DB backend is canonical (probably keep SqliteDb for MVS tier, gate Postgres behind a feature flag).
- Migrate bin/sera.rs router to call into routes/* handlers — delete the inline handlers in bin/sera.rs.
- Resolves D1/D3/D6/D7/D8/D11 in one stroke (duplicates collapse).
- Reconciles sera-r1g8's work (routes/tasks.rs etc. become live).
- Large PR, touches ~60 files, needs careful review.

**Option B — Delete the routes/ tree.**
- Delete routes/, state.rs, services/ entirely (~70 files).
- Port any genuinely useful logic (especially the r1g8 envelope wrapping for tasks/intercom/permission) into inline bin/sera.rs handlers.
- Keep all handlers in bin/sera.rs as the single home — no library split.
- Simpler, smaller PR, but accepts that gateway stays monolithic (no library reuse for tests or external consumers).

## Recommended next steps (regardless of choice)

Before picking A vs B, read:
- bin/sera.rs lines 3037-3100 (router construction + its comment on sqlx incompatibility)
- routes/chat.rs (the most-extended orphan handler) vs bin/sera.rs::chat_handler (~L824)
- state.rs vs bin/sera.rs AppState (~L498)

Then talk to the person who owns the Postgres vs SQLite decision. The duplication is a symptom of an unresolved DB-backend question.

## Blocks / unblocks
- Blocks: sera-4i4i (SessionStore wiring), sera-3rmo (silent failure in chat), sera-qrsh (Op variants), sera-igsd (fail-open policy) — all depend on knowing which handler tree is canonical.
- Unblocks: future development on any HTTP route (so devs stop writing into dead code).

Priority: P1.
notes:
UPDATE 2026-04-23 — pivoted to Option 3 after sera-s31i executor surfaced that routes/ is Postgres-only with disjoint schema from MVS SQLite.

## Revised plan
- sera-vsvz (3l84.1) — MERGED (mod declarations + DbBackend trait, useful for future DB swap even if routes/ gets deleted)
- sera-s31i (3l84.2) — PIVOTED: delete orphan Postgres routes/ + services/; port unique features inline into bin/sera.rs
- sera-utbf (3l84.3) — CLOSED: 'flip binary to thin wrapper' no longer applies; binary stays canonical
- sera-jo8l (3l84.4) — tier: purge, in flight

## Why the pivot
routes/ was written assuming sqlx::PgPool + Postgres schema (agent_instances, chat_messages, api_keys tables). bin/sera.rs MVS uses SqliteDb with a disjoint schema (sessions, transcripts). 'Merging' them requires either a repository trait layer (~800 LOC) or schema migration. Neither aligns with the 'single path with interfaces, config-level backend swap' direction when most of routes/ has no current consumers.

Cheaper: delete the speculative tree, port the genuinely-used features inline. Achieves single-path outcome with less work.

title: CRITICAL: SqliteGitSessionStore not wired into gateway binary — envelopes evaporate on restart
description:
Context: sera-r9ed delivered the SqliteGitSessionStore (PartTable + shadow git) implementation at rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/session_store.rs. sera-r1g8 wired envelope emission into 6 agent-facing routes against Arc<dyn SessionStore>.

**The gap:** rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs defaults to InMemorySessionStore::new() at boot (8+ call sites including main AppState construction). SqliteGitSessionStore is defined, tested, and exposed as public API — but never instantiated in the binary boot path.

**Production impact:** Every running gateway emits envelopes into an in-memory Vec that dies on process restart. The 'auditable + replayable' claim in SPEC-gateway is not met in production — only in tests that explicitly use SqliteGitSessionStore.

**Verification:** Ran scripts/sera-local locally, chatted via /api/chat three times, inspected the data dir. Zero .sqlite files, zero shadow-git dirs anywhere under .sera-local/. The InMemorySessionStore is active.

**Fix scope:**
1. scripts/sera-local needs a --data-dir flag that resolves to a SessionStore config (db_path + sessions_root).
2. bin/sera.rs main AppState construction should instantiate SqliteGitSessionStore::open(db_path, sessions_root) when the Instance manifest or env var specifies a persistence root. Fall back to InMemorySessionStore only for explicit test mode (or remove the in-memory default entirely — fail-closed boot).
3. Decide: should every test AppState construction also use the real impl with a tmpdir, or keep InMemorySessionStore as a test fixture? Probably the latter — keep InMemorySessionStore purely for tests, use SqliteGit in prod.

**Priority: P1** — without this, today's r9ed + r1g8 work provides no production value despite landing.
notes:
Implementation complete — PR pending. Expanded scope based on integration testing (2026-04-23):

## Verified via sera-local
- Started scripts/sera-local, hit /api/chat three times — returned real LM Studio responses.
- Inspected .sera-local/ data dir: ZERO .sqlite files, ZERO shadow git repos. Confirmed InMemorySessionStore is the active impl.
- Confirmed production gap: rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:2734 etc. default Arc::new(InMemorySessionStore::new()) for main AppState + every test AppState.

## RELATED GAP — routes/tasks.rs + routes/intercom.rs + routes/permission_requests.rs ARE NOT BOUND TO THE BINARY ROUTER

Verified via HTTP: /api/agents/sera/tasks, /api/intercom/publish, /api/intercom/dm, /api/permission-requests all return 404. The binary's router in bin/sera.rs lines 3039-3077 mounts /api/chat, /api/a2a/*, /api/agui/*, /api/plugins — but NONE of the r1g8-wrapped routes in routes/{tasks,intercom,permission_requests}.rs.

Consequence: sera-r1g8's envelope emission on tasks/intercom/permission is LITERALLY UNREACHABLE via HTTP in production. Only the chat envelope emission is live, and even that lands in an in-memory store.

## Full Fix Scope (promoted from partial)
1. scripts/sera-local --data-dir support for SessionStore persistence root.
2. bin/sera.rs main AppState instantiation — use SqliteGitSessionStore by default, InMemorySessionStore only in explicit test mode.
3. Bind routes/tasks.rs, routes/intercom.rs, routes/permission_requests.rs into the binary router at the right paths.
4. Decide: is the duplication between bin/sera.rs::chat_handler and routes/chat.rs::chat_handler intentional? If yes, document; if no, pick one. See separate duplicate-audit bead (pending background explore agent report).

Priority stays P1. Code shipped is dead weight until these wires land.

title: Basic memory tier: SQLite FTS5 + sqlite-vec + RRF hybrid (zero-infrastructure RAG)
description:
Implement the zero-infrastructure basic memory tier — a SemanticMemoryStore backed entirely by a single SQLite file combining keyword AND vector search. No Postgres, no pgvector, no external service. Matches the OpenClaw/Hermes 'SQLite-first RAG' pattern.

### Stack

- **Keyword (lexical):** SQLite FTS5 extension, BM25 ranking. Virtual table 'chunks_fts(content, agent_id UNINDEXED, tier UNINDEXED, tags UNINDEXED)'. Query via 'MATCH' + 'bm25(chunks_fts)'.
- **Vector (semantic):** sqlite-vec extension (Alex Garcia). SIMD-accelerated. 'vec0' virtual table 'chunks_vec(embedding float[N])' where N matches the configured embedding provider's dimensionality (default 384 for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 1536 for OpenAI text-embedding-3-small). Distance via 'vec_distance_cosine'.
- **Fusion:** Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) by default — robust, no score-normalisation needed. Weighted-merge fallback (w_vector=0.7, w_bm25=0.3) as a config option for users who prefer tunable weights.
- **Degraded modes:**
  - If sqlite-vec fails to load → log warn!, skip vector side, run BM25-only (still functional).
  - If no embedding provider is configured → vector side is empty, BM25-only (still functional).
  - Never panic, never silently zero-vector a real result.

### Files

- new 'rust/crates/sera-db/src/sqlite_memory_store.rs':
  - 'SqliteMemoryStore { conn: Connection, vec_available: bool, embedding: Option<Arc<dyn EmbeddingService>> }'
  - impl SemanticMemoryStore — put/query/delete/evict/touch/promote/maintenance
  - On 'put': INSERT into main table + chunks_fts; if embedding provider is set, embed content + INSERT into chunks_vec
  - On 'query':
    - BM25 side: SELECT rowid, bm25(chunks_fts) FROM chunks_fts WHERE chunks_fts MATCH ? LIMIT top_k\*2
    - Vector side (if available): SELECT rowid, vec_distance_cosine(embedding, ?) FROM chunks_vec ORDER BY 2 LIMIT top_k\*2
    - Fuse via RRF: rrf_score = sum(1/(k+rank_i)) across both lists (k=60 is the standard constant)
    - Return top_k by fused score with per-signal sub-scores populated in ScoredEntry (index_score, vector_score, recency_score)
  - 'maintenance()': VACUUM + 'INSERT INTO chunks_fts(chunks_fts) VALUES("optimize")' (FTS5 index maintenance); no REINDEX needed
- 'rust/crates/sera-db/Cargo.toml': add 'sqlite-vec' (C extension loader — crate likely provides a small shim); ensure rusqlite features include 'bundled' and 'load_extension'.
- 'rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs': auto-select SqliteMemoryStore for local profile; PgVectorStore when DATABASE_URL + pgvector confirmed; InMemorySemanticStore only for tests.

### Acceptance

- 'cargo test -p sera-db' passes; test suite covers put/query/evict/promote, BM25-only, vec-only, hybrid RRF, and degraded modes.
- A fresh checkout boots 'sera-gateway start' with no DB env vars and can round-trip memory put+query against a SQLite file.
- Benchmark: 10k entries, top-k=5 query under 50ms on a typical dev laptop.
- HybridScorer still reranks cleanly because ScoredEntry carries both index_score and vector_score populated.
- If sqlite-vec isn't present, system logs 'vector recall disabled (sqlite-vec not loaded)' once and continues BM25-only.

Deps: sera-vzz? (local embedding provider — companion bead) for the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 CPU embedding path. Can land with a stub EmbeddingService (NoOp) meanwhile; vector side just stays empty.

title: Local-first data backend: SQLite + files suffice for single-node; Postgres is the enterprise upgrade
description:
Architecture rule: a pure local developer setup must boot with ZERO external databases — SQLite on disk + flat files suffice. Postgres (with pgvector) is the enterprise-scale upgrade, not a hard prereq.

Current state:
- Autonomous mode (sera.yaml + sera-gateway start) already opens 'sera.db' via rusqlite (confirmed via boot log 2026-04-17). Core data uses SQLite already.
- LaneCounter has PostgresLaneCounter / InMemoryLaneCounter fallback — OK.
- ProposalUsageStore has PostgresProposalUsageStore / InMemoryProposalUsageStore fallback — OK.
- Remaining Postgres-only paths (gaps):
  1. PgVectorStore for Tier-2 semantic memory — SQLite/FTS5 backend tracked separately as sera-vzce (basic tier) and sera-syqv (pluggable memory architecture). Plan: keyword-search-first basic tier + documented plugin seam (mem0 / hindsight / RAG as user-installable extensions).
  2. secrets.rs, schedules.rs, audit.rs, metering.rs, agents.rs — sqlx queries, no rusqlite alternative. This bead tracks porting those.

Work (this bead):
- (a) Audit all sqlx call sites in sera-db and port each to a rusqlite equivalent behind the existing abstraction OR introduce a StoreBackend trait so both backends plug in.
- (b) Document the two profiles in docs/ARCHITECTURE: 'local (SQLite + files, single-node)' vs 'enterprise (Postgres + pgvector, multi-pod)'.
- (c) Update docker-compose.rust.yaml to split a 'local' profile (gateway only) from 'enterprise' (+ postgres + centrifugo).

Memory-tier work is split out into sera-vzce (basic tier, P1) and sera-syqv (plugin architecture, P2).

Acceptance: 'sera-gateway start' boots with ONLY a filesystem — no DATABASE_URL, no Postgres, no Centrifugo. All Sprint-1 CLI flows (ping, auth, agent list/show/run) work against this local-only stack.

title: sera-e2e-harness: cross-crate integration test driving full turn loop
description:
Sprint 2 of UX-PLAN.md. Create rust/e2e/ (or module under sera-testing) with at least one --features integration test that:

LOCAL PROFILE (baseline, must pass without any external DB/broker):
1. Boots sera-gateway with SQLite + filesystem only. NO Postgres, NO Centrifugo required. External LLM provider via LLM_BASE_URL (LM Studio / Ollama / OpenAI).
2. Uses sera-cli to auth, spawn an agent, run a turn with a prompt that triggers at least one tool call + one hook.
3. Verifies (always): turn completed, at least one MemoryBlock segment emitted, at least one audit row written to the SQLite store.

ENTERPRISE PROFILE (optional cargo features 'postgres' and/or 'centrifugo'):
4. With 'postgres' feature: swap SQLite store for Postgres + pgvector; run the same assertions; plus verify Tier-2 semantic-memory recall.
5. With 'centrifugo' feature: assert at least one thought event on the expected channel. Skipped (not failed) when absent.

Gated behind --features integration so it does not run on every cargo test.

Acceptance:
- Baseline (no Postgres, no Centrifugo) passes on a fresh checkout with only the gateway binary + SQLite file.
- Adding --features postgres spins up a compose-or-sidecar Postgres and exercises the enterprise path.
- Adding --features centrifugo adds the streaming assertion.
- Runtime under 90s per profile.

Prereq: sera-cli-chat (or at least sera-cli-agent) closed, sera-boot-verify closed, sera-mwb4 (local-first backend) at least partially landed so the baseline profile has a working SqliteSemanticMemoryStore. ~3-4 days.

title: Fix Google/Gemini provider 429 no-body errors via OpenAI compat layer
description: Agents using Google Gemini backend get 429 status code (no body) errors. The Gemini OpenAI compatibility layer may handle rate limiting differently than standard OpenAI. Need to review: 1) How Gemini's OpenAI compat endpoint returns rate limit errors (headers, body format) 2) Whether our LLM proxy correctly parses Gemini 429 responses 3) Whether retry/backoff logic handles the no-body case 4) Reference: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai
notes:
Root cause: Gemini's OpenAI-compat endpoint returns 429 without a 'message' field in the error JSON (or non-JSON body). The OpenAI SDK's makeMessage() in error.js:32 produces '429 status code (no body)' when error?.message is falsy. Pi-mono captures this string and propagates it through the event stream.

The 429 IS detected correctly by is429 checks in LlmRouter.ts and llmProxy.ts (string contains '429'). The chain works but error messages are opaque.

Fix targets:
1. LlmRouter.ts (~line 390, 430): Extract Retry-After header from caught error, pass through
2. llmProxy.ts: Forward retryAfter in 429 JSON response to agent-runtime
3. llmClient.ts (~line 175-178): body['error'] is string 'rate_limited' not object, so errorObj?.['message'] is always undefined — fix the parsing to handle both formats
4. Consider adding a diagnostic curl probe to capture actual Gemini 429 body shape

Design doc reference: see discriminating probe in research notes for exact curl command to reproduce.

title: Optimize context builder for LLM KV cache hit rates
description:
Restructure the agent-runtime context assembly (contextManager, loop.ts, llmClient) to maximize KV cache hit rates across providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini). Design doc: docs/designs/kv-cache-optimization.md

Key anti-patterns found:
1. Time context at priority 60 invalidates 40-60% of system prompt every call (systemPromptBuilder.ts:254-268)
2. Sliding-window compaction shifts prefix, destroying cache (contextManager.ts:552-559)
3. RAG content appended to system prompt makes it volatile (ContextAssembler.ts:244)
4. Zero Anthropic cache_control breakpoints despite parsing cache metrics

Implementation plan (from design doc):
- P0 (1-2 days): Move time-context to priority 135, truncate to hourly, separate RAG into own message
- P1 (1 day): Stepped compaction (drop in groups of 4), alphabetical tool sorting
- P2 (0.5 days): stableStringify with sorted keys for deterministic serialization
- P3 (3-5 days): Anthropic cache_control breakpoints, OpenAI 128-token padding, Gemini Context Caching API

Key files: systemPromptBuilder.ts, ContextAssembler.ts, contextManager.ts, llmClient.ts, json.ts, LlmRouter.ts
notes: Design doc PR: #902. P0+P3.1 delivers ~80% of total improvement. Ready for implementation.

title: Rust shadow proxy — dual-run TS+Rust sera-core with request/response diff
description:
HIGH PRIORITY: Run TypeScript sera-core and Rust sera-core side by side. TS is primary (serves all traffic), Rust receives a copy of every request and responses are compared for parity.

## Architecture

1. **Reverse proxy layer** (nginx or custom Node.js proxy):
   - All requests go to TS sera-core (primary)
   - A copy of each request is forwarded to Rust sera-core (shadow)
   - Responses from both are captured and compared
   - Diffs are logged to a parity report

2. **Parity comparison tool**:
   - Compares HTTP status codes
   - Compares response JSON structure (ignoring timestamps, UUIDs)
   - Compares response body content (semantic diff, not exact match)
   - Flags mismatches with: endpoint, method, request body hash, TS response, Rust response, diff
   - Stores results in DB or file-based log

3. **Dashboard/report**:
   - Parity percentage per endpoint
   - List of failing endpoints with diff details
   - Trend over time (as Rust catches up)

## Implementation Options

**Option A: nginx mirror module**
- nginx mirrors requests to Rust upstream
- Custom log module captures response diffs
- Pro: zero code in either service. Con: response comparison needs a sidecar

**Option B: Node.js proxy (sera-shadow-proxy)**
- Sits in front of both services
- Forwards to TS, copies to Rust
- Compares responses inline
- Pro: full control, rich comparison. Con: adds latency

**Option C: Middleware in TS sera-core**
- After handling each request, fire-and-forget same request to Rust
- Compare responses asynchronously
- Pro: no extra service. Con: couples TS to Rust lifecycle

## Recommendation: Option B
A dedicated proxy gives clean separation and rich comparison without coupling the services.

## Docker Compose Addition
```yaml
sera-shadow-proxy:
  build: ./tools/shadow-proxy
  ports:
    - "3000:3000"  # external port
  environment:
    - PRIMARY_URL=http://sera-core:3001
    - SHADOW_URL=http://sera-core-rs:3001
    - DIFF_LOG_PATH=/data/parity-diffs.jsonl
```

## Prerequisites
- Rust sera-core must compile and start (fix Cargo.toml edition error)
- Wire services into AppState
- At minimum: health endpoint + a few simple GET routes responding
notes: Rust compiles with rustls (no OpenSSL needed). Shadow proxy Dockerfile created. docker-compose.yaml updated with sera-shadow-proxy service enabled. Merge conflict with main resolved. PR #847 updated and pushed.

title: Gated skill/tool loading — context-aware activation
description:
Sera's tool/skill set needs context-window-aware gating. Currently all tools are loaded into context permanently, wasting tokens. Need a system where:

## Problem
- All tools (26 principles, ~16 tools) load into every conversation
- Orchestration tools (delegate-task, bridge routing) waste context when user is just chatting
- As capabilities grow, the system prompt will exceed context limits

## Proposed Solution: Gated Skills
- Skills/tools have activation triggers (keywords, explicit /commands, or sera decides)
- When activated: tool definitions + relevant principles load into context
- When deactivated: tools and principles leave context
- Always-on tools: knowledge-store, knowledge-query, web-search (core to sera's identity)
- Gated tools: orchestration (bridges, metrics, dogfeed), file operations, shell-exec, scheduling

## Skill Groups
- **core** (always on): knowledge, web search, memory
- **orchestration** (gated): delegate-task to bridges, metrics, dogfeed, task routing
- **devtools** (gated): file-read, shell-exec, code analysis
- **scheduling** (gated): schedule-task, cron management
- **admin** (gated): agent management, provider config, channel management

## Research
- Investigate how claw-code (clawhip's predecessor) handled gated tool loading
- Look at Claude Code's skill activation pattern as reference
- Consider: should sera self-activate skills based on conversation context, or require explicit activation?

## Implementation Considerations
- IdentityService.generateSystemPrompt() needs to support dynamic tool sets
- Tool definitions sent to LLM must be filterable per-turn
- Skill activation state stored in session (not persistent across conversations unless sera decides)
- Token budget tracking: measure how much context each skill group consumes
design: Minimal diff approach: 1 new manifest field (tools.skillGroups), 1 lookup table (TOOL_GROUPS in definitions.ts), 1 function (selectActiveGroups in loop.ts), 1 call site change (filter in run() before refreshSystemPrompt). 3-layer activation: manifest-declared groups > task keyword regex triggers > existing tool-search fallback. Files: definitions.ts, manifest.ts, loop.ts, agent-template.v1.json. Saves ~55% on tool-related tokens (~1800 tokens/call). Always-on: tool-search, skill-search, knowledge-store, knowledge-query.

title: user chat should handle empty assistant message without raw provider error
description:
Transcript evidence: `/home/entity/.hermes/cache/documents/doc_b3dc7ae83606_message.txt`.

Observed failure:
When Sebastian asked `so no skill discovery at all?`, the Discord conversation returned a raw runtime/provider failure:

`[LLM error: LLM call failed: request error: provider returned assistant message with neither content nor tool_calls]`

Why this matters:
An operator-facing agent must not expose raw provider failure strings as the final assistant response. Empty assistant messages with no content and no tool calls are a known provider/model edge case; SERA should classify it, retry when safe, and otherwise produce a compact blocked/failed card or user-facing explanation with audit evidence.

Suggested scope:
- Locate the LLM response normalization path in the runtime/gateway connector path.
- Add handling for assistant messages that contain neither content nor tool calls.
- Decide minimal behavior: retry once if idempotent/safe; otherwise return a structured blocked/failed turn outcome rather than raw provider text.
- Preserve detailed provider error in logs/audit, not as the user-visible answer.
- Add regression coverage using a fake provider response with empty assistant content/tool_calls.

Acceptance:
- Empty assistant message with no content/tool calls does not surface raw `LLM call failed... neither content nor tool_calls` to Discord/user chat.
- The turn outcome is classified as retryable/blocked/failed with a concise user-facing message and evidence/audit id where available.
- A regression test/fake provider fixture covers the exact edge case.
- Logs/audit retain the raw provider detail for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Assistant message with neither content nor tool_calls is retried or converted into structured blocked/failed outcome; raw provider error is not user-visible; logs/audit retain raw detail; regression fake-provider test covers the exact edge case.

title: agent self-introspection should report real workspace, container, tools, and skill discovery state
description:
Transcript evidence: `/home/entity/.hermes/cache/documents/doc_b3dc7ae83606_message.txt`.

Observed failures from live SERA Discord chat:
1. When asked workspace/environment, the agent listed `/root` and WSL2 but failed to recognize Docker/container context until Sebastian corrected it.
2. When asked `what skills do you have access to?`, the agent answered only from `allowed_tools` in `sera.yaml`, with no real skill discovery or explicit statement that skills are not discoverable/configured.
3. When asked `so no skill discovery at all?`, the chat surfaced a raw provider/runtime error: `LLM call failed: request error: provider returned assistant message with neither content nor tool_calls`.

Why this matters:
Operator trust depends on SERA being able to inspect and explain its actual runtime environment and capabilities. If it cannot discover skills, it should say that truthfully and name the configured tool/capability surface. It should not hallucinate WSL vs Docker, and it should not leak raw LLM provider errors into the user conversation.

Suggested scope for capability/workspace introspection:
- Add or expose a small introspection path that can answer:
  - current workspace/root and relevant files.
  - container vs host/WSL evidence, using probes such as `/.dockerenv`, hostname, cgroup, and kernel.
  - configured agent, provider/model, allowed tools, and whether a `sera-skills` registry/source is available.
- If skill discovery is absent, answer explicitly: no skill registry/discovery is currently wired for this runtime; configured allowed tools are X.
- Keep secrets redacted.
- Add an integration/smoke test or fixture conversation for the questions in the transcript.

Acceptance:
- Live agent/API can answer workspace/environment using actual probes and identifies Docker-on-WSL when applicable.
- Live agent/API can answer skill/capability question from a real discovery/config path, including explicit `no skill discovery wired` if that is current truth.
- Output distinguishes tools, skills, model/provider, memory, and sessions; it does not collapse all into generic capabilities.
- Secrets are redacted.
- Regression coverage includes the transcript questions.
acceptance_criteria: Live agent/API answers workspace/environment and skill/capability questions from actual probes/config; Docker-on-WSL is identified when applicable; absence of skill discovery is explicit; tools/skills/provider/model/memory/sessions are distinguished; secrets redacted; transcript questions covered by regression/smoke.

title: sera-gateway: /api/chat stream:true silently emits done(0 tokens) on empty runtime reply
description:
The streaming branch of chat_handler at rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:1381 has no empty-reply guard. When execute_turn returns reply="" (e.g. reasoning model exhausted max_tokens, runtime LLM call failed silently, etc.), the SSE stream emits zero 'message' events followed by a 'done' event with usage=0/0/0. The web client renders this as a stuck 'thinking…' state with no error.

The sync path at line 1561 already handles this case correctly with HTTP 502 + JSON error body. The streaming path needs equivalent behavior: emit an SSE 'error' event with the same shape, then close.

Repro (with sera-gateway running and a misbehaving runtime path):
- POST /api/chat {agent, message, stream: true} → returns 200 with only an event:done frame, no message frames.
- POST /api/chat {agent, message, stream: false} → correctly returns 502 {error: 'runtime returned empty reply'}.

Fix:
- Add the empty-reply check after execute_turn in the streaming branch (line 1431-ish).
- Emit an SSE 'error' event ({code, message}) and transition to StreamState::Done so the stream terminates cleanly.
- Web client (web/src/lib/api.ts parseChatSseEvent) extends ChatStreamEvent with an 'error' variant.
- Web ChatView surfaces the error to the user rather than spinning forever.

title: [architecture decision] Workflow task storage split — InMemoryWorkflowTaskStore vs WorkflowEngine durable
description:
From duplicate implementation audit 2026-04-29:
- sera-workflow::engine::WorkflowEngine — async orchestrator with claim/heartbeat/recover_orphans, durable SQLite + in-memory backends.
- sera-gateway::workflow_store::InMemoryWorkflowTaskStore — in-memory only, wraps sera_workflow::WorkflowTask in its own WorkflowTaskRecord adding agent_id, resume_token, SchedulerTaskStatus.

Phase 1 explicitly says persistent storage is a follow-up; gateway will eventually want durability and at that point both layers fight.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: extend WorkflowEngine model with scheduler-side fields, or document gateway store as a thin in-memory cache layered above the engine. Migration plan recorded for durable gateway scheduler state. SPEC-gateway / SPEC-workflow updated to name the canonical owner of each field.
notes: Decision: KEEP SEPARATE. ADR landed in docs/public/decisions/2026-05-02-workflow-storage.md. PR #1178. Two stores model orthogonal lifecycles over the same WorkflowTask payload: (a) sera-workflow::WorkflowEngine owns claim/dispatch (Open->Hooked->Closed, atomic CAS, orphan reaper) - zero call sites outside its own crate today; (b) sera-gateway::WorkflowTaskStore owns gate/resume (Pending->Resolved + agent_id/resume_token routing). Reasons not to consolidate: distinct status surfaces, distinct schema fields, distinct write cadences, premature refactor on engine that has no caller, and consolidating would invert dispatch-ownership ADR's embedded-mode framing. Follow-ups filed in ADR section 5 (cross-store reconciler + revisit-merge once both stores have real callers).

The point is to force the taxonomic decisions (Pattern A vs B per harness) to be concrete — there is no way to ship M1 without picking a transport per harness type and writing the registration handshake.

Not implementable in isolation; depends on sera-5mbr (Stdio transport), sera-w2dh (tool catalog), sera-eq0m (egress restriction), sera-kg3g (clawhip launcher inference.local), sera-pcvp (Op::Register Pattern B), and sera-40y3 (kill switch teardown).

Hermes ACP server spawns as a Stdio child of the gateway via sera-5mbr; its tool catalog registers and aliases via sera-w2dh; a probe call confirms tool dispatch returns through the gateway. 3. clawhip-launched 'claude code' tmux session is started with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://inference.local:443 (sera-kg3g) and a one-shot SERA token; registers via sera-pcvp Op::Register as ExternalAgentPrincipal with protocol=A2A. 4. title: [bug] sera-gateway: /api/chat stream:true does not cancel execute_turn when SSE client disconnects
description: rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:1417 registers a CancellationToken via state.register_cancellation_token but execute_turn at line 1419 is awaited inside the unfold's first iteration without any select-against-disconnect or token.cancelled() observation. Combined with the buffered fake-stream architecture (sera-k8do), a client that drops the SSE socket mid-turn causes execute_turn to run to completion server-side — full LLM tokens consumed, transcript persisted, lane held — before the unfold notices the broken pipe and stops.\n\nDistinct from sera-mplr (POST /api/chat/cancel — explicit client-side cancel verb): this is the implicit cancel via TCP/SSE disconnect that every browser/curl already provides. Without it, refreshing a page or closing a tab still bills the user for the rest of the turn.
acceptance_criteria: 1) execute_turn must accept a CancellationToken (or equivalent) and check it inside its turn loop, not only at the top. 2) chat_handler must connect the SSE stream's drop to that token — axum's Sse with KeepAlive surfaces 'client gone' as a Stream::poll error; convert that to token.cancel(). 3) Integration test: open SSE, drop after first delta, assert that within 2s the runtime cancellation event fires and no further LLM calls are attempted. 4) Coordinate with sera-mplr on the cancel verb so both paths share one cancellation primitive.
close_reason: Merged PR #1150 (5c5f8f50, head repair c4cb143b): SSE disconnect cancellation and JoinError cleanup share cancellation/lane cleanup primitive; checks green.

title: sera-gateway: runtime child has no supervisor; one panic kills the agent for the lifetime of the gateway pod
description: StdioHarness::spawn (rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:218) is one-shot. The gateway calls it once per agent at boot (3535-3543), inserts the harness into AppState.harnesses, and never re-spawns. If the runtime child crashes (e.g. unhandled panic in a tool, OOM in context_engine, BrokenPipe on a flaky network), every subsequent /api/chat or Discord message returns BrokenPipe with a child_exit_context message and ops have to restart the gateway pod. The gateway already has rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/process_manager.rs (ProcessManager, RestartPolicy, SpawnRequest) that is dead in the production binary. Investigation: either (a) wrap StdioHarness via ProcessManager and set RestartPolicy on it, or (b) add a per-harness supervisor task that observes child.try_wait()/exit_status and re-spawns into AppState.harnesses with backoff. Scope: medium — involves Arc<RwLock<>> on AppState.harnesses, careful drain semantics on shutdown, and bounded backoff to avoid thrash.
acceptance_criteria: Killing the runtime PID externally causes the next chat call to succeed within 2s after respawn (or fail with a clearly differentiated error). Boot/recover log emits harness:<agent>:respawned with attempt count. Bounded backoff (e.g. exponential up to N=5 then sticky failure surface). Existing tests pass. New test exercises kill+next-turn-succeeds. cargo clippy -D warnings clean.
notes: Implementation landed in PR #1123 — fix/sera-ojp3-runtime-supervisor. Adds RuntimeChildSupervisor per agent (lazy try_wait + mark_unhealthy + bounded shutdown). Covers cold-crash, in-flight crash, and post-turn exit windows. cargo test -p sera-gateway: 284 passed; cargo check --workspace: clean; clippy -D warnings: clean. Not closing until PR merges.

title: feat(scripts/sera-omc): point launched tmux panes at inference.local proxy
description: scripts/sera-omc and scripts/sera-omx wrap Claude Code / Codex sessions in clawhip-monitored tmux. Today they pass the operator's own ANTHROPIC/OPENAI keys straight through, so every turn billed to the user's account bypasses the gateway's universal LLM proxy (SPEC-gateway §13a). For SERA to be the compliance boundary the launcher must (a) export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/OPENAI_BASE_URL pointing at the gateway's inference.local, (b) mint a one-shot SERA-issued token bound to the session's budget, (c) unset or rotate the operator's own API keys for the duration of the session.
design: Pattern B integration. The launcher is the enforcement point for sessions that run on the host (not inside a SERA-managed sandbox). Strict mode: refuse to launch when the gateway is unreachable. Soft mode (current dev default): warn-and-continue but mark the session as non-compliant in clawhip Discord notifications.
acceptance_criteria: A clawhip-launched Claude Code or Codex session never reaches Anthropic/OpenAI directly when SERA gateway is up. All LLM turns from that session appear in the gateway proxy audit log with the session's principal. Acceptance test: tcpdump (or strace) on the launcher shows zero outbound TCP to api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com; gateway audit shows N requests for N visible turns.
notes:
Cross-refs: artifacts/handoffs/omc-sera-j3kv-clawhip-monitoring.md (clawhip wrapper history), SPEC-gateway §13a, report §3.5 / §5 B7. Pairs with sera-eq0m for the in-sandbox enforcement variant.
Blocked in strict acceptance by missing egress manifest vocabulary and gateway inference.local proxy. See artifacts/reports/research/eq0m-egress-restriction-scout-2026-04-30.md §3 PR E.
close_reason: Implemented by merged PR #1152 / eb9f2e3a: OMC/OMX launcher inference.local proxy routing with PROXY_RC review fix.

title: sera-{gateway,runtime}: dispatch-ownership drift — code dispatches tools in runtime, SPEC-gateway 1b says gateway
description: SPEC-gateway.md section 1b states unambiguously: 'Tool dispatch belongs entirely to the gateway. The harness never holds credentials.' SPEC-runtime.md section 1a section 3 reinforces: the runtime 'forwards tool call events to the gateway' and 'does NOT execute tools.' Production code does the opposite: rust/crates/sera-runtime owns LlmClient, TraitToolRegistry (14 built-ins), and RegistryDispatcher::dispatch (rust/crates/sera-runtime/src/tools/dispatcher.rs:138). The gateway only observes ToolCallBegin/End events post-hoc for audit. enforce_tool_events at bin/sera.rs:2004 explicitly notes 'Pre-dispatch enforcement now lives in sera-runtime.' This is a major spec-vs-code drift that will mislead anyone reading the spec to add a custom tool or build a Tier-2 deployment. Decision needed: either (a) document the MVS deviation as a deployment-mode choice (local/pet keeps dispatch in runtime; enterprise/cattle moves it to gateway), or (b) plan the migration to gateway-side dispatch behind a feature flag. Investigation: review SPEC-gateway 1b/1c, SPEC-runtime 1a/3, SPEC-tools 6 for consistency; pick a path; write an ADR.
acceptance_criteria: SPEC-runtime 1a (or new ADR under docs/plan/decisions/) explicitly names the runtime-side dispatch mode and references the StdioHarness MVS path. Gateway boots log dispatch_mode={runtime,gateway} per agent. SPEC-gateway 1b updated or annotated with deployment-mode applicability. No code changes required for option (a).
notes: PR #1121 repair lane pr1121-y45a-review-repair is resolving Codex review 3165755992 and rebasing after PR #1123 conflict. Keep open until branch pushed, CI green, and review comments clear.
close_reason: Completed in PR #1121: dispatch ownership ADR/spec annotations plus honest effective runtime dispatch-mode boot logging after Codex review repair and rebase onto #1123.

title: [bug] sera-runtime: sera-hitl P1-INTEGRATION points (security_analyzer, assessment, tool_result, ask_for_approval) not wired into turn pipeline
description:
Four files in sera-hitl carry 'TODO P1-INTEGRATION' markers explicitly stating they are not yet wired into the runtime turn loop:

title: sera-gateway: agent-manifest tools.allow not forwarded to runtime child; LLM sees every built-in tool
description: When the gateway spawns the sera-runtime child (rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:3505-3543), it forwards LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL, LLM_API_KEY, AGENT_ID, SERA_AGENT_POLICY_REF, SERA_CAPABILITY_POLICIES_DIR — but never the agent's tools.allow/deny list from AgentSpec. The runtime then calls TraitToolRegistry::with_builtins_and_authz unconditionally (rust/crates/sera-runtime/src/main.rs:218 + tools/mod.rs:72-87) and exposes all 14 built-ins to the LLM via tool_defs. CapabilityRegistry blocks execution post-call, but the LLM has already been steered by the visible tool list — and prompt-window tokens are wasted on tools the agent isn't supposed to see. Investigation: confirm the AgentSpec field shape in sera-types/src/config_manifest.rs, then add a SERA_AGENT_TOOLS_ALLOW env var (comma-separated globs) consumed in main.rs after with_builtins. Scope: small — env wiring + glob filter + tests.
acceptance_criteria: With manifest tools.allow: ["memory_*"], tool_defs returned to the LLM contains only memory_* entries. Unit test on the glob filter (allow precedence, deny override). Integration test boots gateway with restricted manifest and asserts LLM-visible tool names. CapabilityRegistry behavior unchanged. cargo clippy -D warnings clean.
close_reason: Merged PR #1119 (5237f032): gateway forwards tools.allow/tools.deny to runtime and runtime preserves documented legacy tool patterns. CI green.

title: feat(sera-gateway): tool-catalog reconciliation for BYOH harness registration
description: SPEC-tools §717 says when a BYOH harness (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes) connects, the gateway augments the harness's tool schema with sera-managed tools. The collision algorithm is undefined: today a harness with its own 'Read' tool and a SERA gateway with 'read_file' can produce silent dual-dispatch, capability laundering (harness uses internal tool, bypassing AuthZ + audit), or argument-shape mismatch on alias. This is a compliance hole — every BYOH integration with overlapping tools is a candidate for it.
design: Pattern A only — Pattern B sessions do not share a tool catalog with the gateway (see report §3.2). Algorithm: gateway computes name_map(harness_name → canonical_name) at registration; harness must suppress aliased internal implementations and emit aliased calls via SQ/EQ. Probe is a registration-time test, not a runtime check.
acceptance_criteria: At registration the harness submits a tool catalog; the gateway returns a rewritten catalog with a name map (harness_name → canonical_name). A poison-tool probe verifies the harness routes the aliased call back through SQ/EQ. Test: harness with internal 'Read' + gateway with 'read_file' produces exactly one read_file invocation through gateway dispatch; the harness's internal Read is provably bypassed.
notes:
References: SPEC-tools §717, SPEC-gateway §1b, report §3.2 / §5 B3.
2026-05-01: PR #1151 merged (57039bae) with pure reconciliation core: HarnessToolDecl/HarnessCatalog/GatewayToolDecl/ReconciledCatalog, deterministic collision/name_map policy, poison-tool/capability-laundering unit coverage. Remaining before closing this bead: registration RPC/handshake that accepts harness catalog, returns rewritten catalog/name_map, plumbs reconciled catalog through AppState, and proves an aliased harness call is dispatched through SQ/EQ rather than the internal tool.
close_reason: Implemented by merged PR #1154 / 9753608b: BYOH registration handshake and reconciled tool catalog poison-probe acceptance.

title: feat(sera-gateway): wire Stdio variant of AppServerTransport
description: AppServerTransport enum at rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/transport/mod.rs:23 declares InProcess/Stdio/WebSocket/Grpc/WebhookBack but only InProcess is wired (line 87). The existing StdioHarness implementation at rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:209 already manages a long-running sera-runtime child via stdin/stdout NDJSON; it just is not reachable from the typed transport enum. Wiring this is the largest gap blocking Pattern A BYOH harnesses (Hermes ACP, sera-byoh-agent) from registering against the gateway via SPEC-gateway §7a. Without this, every BYOH integration has to monkey-patch the bin.
design: Pattern A path. Reuse StdioHarness in rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:209 — do not write a parallel harness. Pull it out of the bin into a transport submodule under sera-gateway/src/transport/stdio.rs so the bin only owns wiring. Per SPEC-gateway §7a the JSON-RPC envelope is identical across transports; this PR is plumbing, not protocol design.
acceptance_criteria: AppServerTransport::Stdio { command, args, env } variant is wired through the gateway registration path. Integration test in sera-gateway spawns sera-byoh-agent (rust/crates/sera-byoh-agent) as a Stdio child and round-trips a UserTurn through the SQ/EQ envelope. Test verifies the child is reaped on KillSwitch (cross-ref sera-40y3).
notes: PR #1143: https://github.com/TKCen/sera/pull/1143 — AppServerTransport::Stdio factory wired to StdioTransport. Bin StdioHarness deferred (different abstraction; needs follow-up bead).
close_reason: Merged PR #1143 (b1ee03a): AppServerTransport::Stdio factory wired to StdioTransport; child kill_on_drop added; broader StdioHarness unification remains follow-up.

title: [bug] sera-gateway: /api/chat stream:true is buffered fake-streaming, not real LLM streaming
description: rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:1380-1531 (chat_handler SSE branch) executes the full execute_turn synchronously, splits result.reply by spaces (split_inclusive(' ')), and only after the turn completes does it emit those word chunks as SSE events. The user's perceived TTFT is identical to a non-streaming response — the server holds the entire reply, then dribbles it out post-hoc.\n\nNote: existing sera-1uox describes a 'no intermediate delta' symptom; this issue is the underlying architectural defect — streaming must come from llm_client.chat() (which already supports SSE per src/llm_client.rs#parse_sse_data_line) rather than being faked after the fact. The fake stream also explains why result.usage is correct here but the bytes wire-shape gives no early-tokens.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Decide whether stream:true should plumb tokens through from runtime stdio events or call llm_client.chat() directly with stream=true. 2) Replace post-hoc split_inclusive with a Stream<TurnEvent> that yields delta frames as the LLM emits them. 3) Integration test (mock_lm_studio_test style) verifies first delta arrives < 500ms after request even when total reply takes >2s. 4) Update sera-1uox once architecture lands; close it as a fix-by-side-effect or leave separate per maintainer call.
notes:
2026-05-01: PR #1150 closed sera-7mc1 cancellation/cleanup half only. Real token streaming remains open: replace post-hoc split_inclusive fake streaming with LLM/runtime delta stream and TTFT regression test.
Close reason correction: implemented by merged PR #1153 / 6284bd18; real /api/chat SSE delta streaming with review repairs for mid-stream error, cancellation, and bounded delta queue.
close_reason: Implemented by merged PR #1153 / $(gh pr view 1153 --repo TKCen/sera --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid | cut -c1-8): real /api/chat SSE delta streaming with review repairs for mid-stream error, cancellation, and bounded delta queue.

title: [bug] [security-p2] sera-auth: JwtService::default silently mints ephemeral random secret when SERA_JWT_SECRET unset
description: rust/crates/sera-auth/src/jwt.rs:119-135 'impl Default for JwtService' falls back to a random 32-byte secret when SERA_JWT_SECRET is missing or empty, and only logs a tracing::warn. This is a silent foot-gun: a misconfigured production deploy still issues and verifies tokens, but every restart invalidates every issued token, and any sibling pod has a different secret so tokens minted by one are unverifiable by another. The Default impl is also referenced from #[test] (line 222) so adding a hard error on missing env requires test plumbing.\n\nReproduction: unset SERA_JWT_SECRET and call JwtService::default(); the warn fires but the service is functional. Inspecting downstream usage in gateway: nothing checks the JwtService for 'is_ephemeral'.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Decide policy: prod must hard-error when SERA_JWT_SECRET unset; tests use JwtService::for_tests() with explicit secret. 2) Implement JwtService::from_env() -> Result<Self, AuthError::MissingJwtSecret>; deprecate or restrict Default. 3) Audit AppState construction in sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs to call from_env() and surface a startup error. 4) New unit test asserts from_env() errors when env unset. 5) Document the behavior in rust/CLAUDE.md learnings.
notes: PR #1140 https://github.com/TKCen/sera/pull/1140 — replaced Default impl with from_env()/for_tests(), added AuthError::MissingJwtSecret. Gateway binary has no current JwtService construction site; library-side fix prevents any future caller from silently using ephemeral keys.
close_reason: Merged PR #1140 (aadc0b3): removed JwtService::default foot-gun; added from_env()/for_tests() and MissingJwtSecret.

title: feat(web): thin operator console for rust gateway (parent)
description:
Build a minimal React SPA covering only what sera-gateway exposes today. Not a port of legacy/web — a fresh, narrow surface that doubles as an E2E forcing function for endpoint expansion.

SCOPE (Sprint 1, this bead's children):
- Page set: Dashboard (health), Chat (live AG-UI SSE), Agents (list/detail), Sessions (list + transcript viewer), Hooks (read-only list).
- Out of scope (Sprint 2+): Memory explorer, audit, schedules, circles, introspection, orchestration, killswitch admin (admin server is on a different port — separate auth model).

STACK PICKS (default — flag now if wrong):
- React 19 + Vite 6 + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + TanStack Query 5
- react-router 7 (data router)
- @microsoft/fetch-event-source for SSE (better than EventSource: supports Authorization header)
- shadcn/ui primitives via Radix (matches legacy idiom; saves design time)
- Vitest for unit tests, Playwright already configured at e2e/ for E2E
- NO Centrifugo dependency (deferred — gateway doesn't expose it locally; AG-UI SSE is sufficient for v1)

Login page accepts a key, validates against /api/auth/me, persists, attaches Authorization header to all subsequent requests.

GATEWAY ROUTES AVAILABLE TODAY (16 public):
- /api/health, /api/health/ready

title: CapabilityPolicy: move enforcement into sera-runtime for true pre-dispatch
description:
Follow-up to sera-ifjl (PR #1070). Gateway-side enforcement now rewrites denied tool_call_begin/end pairs into explicit denials and emits audit entries, but the sera-runtime child process has already begun tool execution by the time the gateway observes the begin event. For true pre-dispatch blocking (tool does not run at all on denial), the CapabilityRegistry needs to be consulted inside sera-runtime before the tool invocation, not after.

Scope:
- Expose CapabilityRegistry (or equivalent) to sera-runtime (pass policy via spawn env, or have runtime read the same SERA_CAPABILITY_POLICIES_DIR)
- Check in the runtime's tool dispatch path (wherever tools are actually invoked in sera-runtime)
- Surface denials through the existing NDJSON error channel so the gateway does not need the post-hoc rewrite anymore
- Remove the gateway-side rewrite once the runtime path is live, keeping only the audit emission in the gateway as a defense-in-depth check

Related: PR #1070 (sera-ifjl), capability_enforcement.rs module comment.

title: feat(sera-gateway): kill harness subprocess on KillSwitch ROLLBACK
description: sera-bsem (PR #1069) cancels in-flight futures but does NOT kill the sera-runtime child process. On DISARM-and-resume without a gateway restart, the harness's BufReader still points at a stdout pipe containing a stale TurnCompleted frame from the aborted turn — the next submission will read the previous turn's reply as its own. SPEC §7a.4 intends ROLLBACK to be followed by process restart, but a safer implementation would: (a) call child.kill() on every registered harness after cancel_all_in_flight, or (b) mark harnesses as dirty and respawn on DISARM before accepting submissions. Either prevents state corruption when an operator issues ROLLBACK then DISARM without restarting the process.
notes: PR: https://github.com/TKCen/sera/pull/1173

title: sera-memory: no cross-backend contract test suite for SemanticMemoryStore trait

The DB-backed PgVector round-trip is explicitly gated behind cfg(feature = 'integration') with no integration fixture present in the workspace. Reproducer: grep -rn 'impl SemanticMemoryStore' rust/crates/ -- shows 4 production impls, none exercised by a shared contract test macro/suite.
notes: Contract suite created in rust/crates/sera-memory/src/contract_tests.rs. InMemorySemanticStore passes all 13 contracts. SqliteMemoryStore passes 11/13; scope_filter and hierarchical_query contracts are opted out because bm25_probe/vec_probe do not apply SemanticQuery::scope as a SQL WHERE predicate — confirmed gap. Fix: add scope_kind/scope_key filter to bm25_probe and vec_probe in sqlite_store.rs, then remove ContractOptions opt-outs.

Retire detect_flagged_operation once ApprovalRouter is wired.

title: POST /api/chat: 429 response has empty body and no Retry-After header
description: When /api/chat returns 429 Too Many Requests (lane occupied by active turn), the response body is empty (content-length: 0) and no Retry-After header is included. Clients have no way to distinguish this from a transient rate limit vs a permanent lane wedge, and no guidance on when to retry. Expected: JSON error body like {"error": "turn in progress", "session_id": "...", "retry_after": N} and a Retry-After header. curl repro: TOKEN=605d685d...; trigger a long-running turn, then immediately: curl -sv -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"message": "hello", "stream": true}' → HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests, content-length: 0 (no body, no Retry-After).

title: POST /api/chat: missing 'message' field returns 422 not 400

Expected: HTTP 400 Bad Request with a structured JSON error body. The raw deserialization error is leaked directly to the client without a structured error envelope. curl repro: TOKEN=605d685d...; curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' → 422 with plain text error string.

title: POST /api/chat: doom-loop response wedges session lane until container restart
description: When the agent runtime detects a doom loop (3 consecutive act cycles), it returns a response with body '[interrupted: doom loop: 3 consecutive act cycles]' and HTTP 200. However, the session lane is left in is_processing=true state — all subsequent /api/chat requests return 429 'queued behind active turn' until the container is restarted. The lane counter is not properly released after a doom-loop interruption. CLAUDE.md learning confirms: 'a hung runtime... never returns, so the caller never calls complete_run, and the session lane stays is_processing=true until container restart'. Repro: POST /api/chat {"message": "hello"} → observe doom-loop response. All subsequent POSTs to /api/chat return 429 indefinitely. curl repro: TOKEN=605d685d...; curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"message": "hello"}'; curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"message": "hello again"}' → 429
notes:
ROOT CAUSE TRACE (tracer 2026-04-24):

FAILURE SIGNATURE: 'Chat message queued behind active turn' (429) repeating 04:54:56–04:58:42 on session http:sera:ses_18a91976f764dcf700000001. Cleared only by runtime shutdown @04:59:05 + respawn @04:59:07 (docker restart of the runtime child).

CONCLUSION: HTTP /api/chat path ALREADY releases the lane on every exit path:
  - Envelope persist fail → release_lane @sera.rs:987
  - HITL flag → release_lane @sera.rs:997
  - Transcript append fail → release_lane @sera.rs:1011
  - Normal return after execute_turn → release_lane @sera.rs:1196 (BEFORE the 502 empty-reply guard at 1202). So even the empty-reply 502 path does NOT wedge.
  - SSE streaming path → complete_run @sera.rs:1086 before persisting.

THE WEDGE IS NOT IN CHAT. IT IS IN STEER INJECTION PATH — NO TIMEOUT.

Evidence: execute_steer at sera.rs:1596-1647 calls harness.stdin.write_all, then loops on stdout.read_line WITHOUT tokio::time::timeout. Contrast execute_turn at sera.rs:1555 which wraps send_turn in tokio::time::timeout(turn_timeout(), …). If the runtime hangs mid-turn (e.g. after the empty-reply FinalOutput from sera-8h23 leaves the child's stdout loop in an odd state, or the model stalls on a steer prompt, or LM Studio drops the connection), execute_steer blocks forever, and the complete_run call at sera.rs:2114 is never reached → lane stays is_processing=true → all subsequent admissions return EnqueueResult::Queued → 429.

Additionally: execute_steer also does .unwrap() on write_all/flush at sera.rs:1618-1619 — a runtime crash during steer would panic the gateway task instead of releasing the lane.

SECOND RISK (not the primary wedge): after execute_turn emits a FinalOutput via the runtime, the runtime's stdio loop (stdio.rs:147-264) emits all events for this turn and returns to the top of the loop. No persistent corruption there. So the only path that can wedge after normal chat completion is a follow-up steer injection while the runtime is unreachable, OR a hung turn longer than 600s (turn_timeout default) also wedges — but the timeout normally covers that.

RE-READING THE CLAUDE.md LEARNING: 'a hung runtime... never returns, so the caller never calls complete_run, and the session lane stays is_processing=true until container restart'. Exactly matches execute_steer's untimed read_line.

FIX SCOPE:
A) sera.rs:1596 execute_steer — wrap stdout.read_line loop in tokio::time::timeout(turn_timeout(), …). On elapsed: log + bail. Callers must call complete_run unconditionally (already true at sera.rs:2114).
B) sera.rs:1618-1619 replace .unwrap() on write_all/flush with ? / bail — same pattern as send_turn:242-247 (child_exit_context diagnostic).
C) Defensive: wrap every execute_steer call in process_message within a scope that ALWAYS calls complete_run via a RAII guard or explicit drop-guard — covers steer panics.

THIS BUG IS THE CASCADE. The leaf is the runtime empty-response (sera-8h23). A fixed empty-reply path reduces the surface that can trigger wedge, but the untimed execute_steer is the mechanism that makes the wedge survive until container restart.

PATCH PLAN:
1. [LEAF/sera-8h23] rust/crates/sera-runtime/src/llm_client.rs — around line 451: if choice.message.content.is_none() && choice.message.tool_calls is None-or-empty, return LlmError::RequestError('provider returned empty assistant message with no tool calls'). OR in turn.rs:647: if response string is empty AND tokens.total==0 AND no tool_calls, promote to TurnOutcome::Interruption{reason:'provider returned empty response'}. Test: unit test in turn.rs mocking LlmProvider to return content:None.
2. [CASCADE/sera-xk8d] rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:1596-1647 execute_steer — add tokio::time::timeout wrapper with turn_timeout(), replace unwraps with ?, return Result. Test: extend send_turn_times_out_when_harness_hangs-style test for execute_steer (spawn_mock_hang harness, assert returns within timeout, assert complete_run called).
3. [DEFENSE] consider refactoring lane-slot release into LaneRunGuard (RAII) to remove the 'caller must release' footgun across all 7+ complete_run call sites.

LINKED EVIDENCE: empty-reply error log at 2026-04-24T05:00:14 maps to session that had already been issuing 429s since 04:54:56, strongly suggesting the wedge came FIRST, then the runtime was shutdown/restarted, and the first post-restart turn on the new runtime returned empty — two independent bugs, both on the same session, interleaved.

title: POST /api/chat: second consecutive turn returns 502 (runtime empty reply)
description: The second POST /api/chat on the same session returns HTTP 502 with body {"error":"runtime returned empty reply"}. Gateway log: 'execute_turn returned empty reply; runtime produced no text'. Repro: 1) POST /api/chat {"message": "My favorite color is purple"} → 200 OK. 2) Immediately POST /api/chat {"message": "What is my favorite color?"} → 502. Gateway log shows tool_events_count=0, tools_ran=false, all token counts 0. The runtime produces no NDJSON output for the second turn. curl repro: TOKEN=605d685d...; curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"message": "My favorite color is purple"}'; sleep 1; curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"message": "What is my favorite color?"}'
notes:
ROOT CAUSE TRACE (tracer 2026-04-24):

FAILURE SIGNATURE @05:00:14: 'execute_turn returned empty reply; runtime produced no text, prompt_tokens=0, completion_tokens=0, tool_events_count=0'. Full zero across the board, no runtime-side TurnStarted/StreamingDelta/TurnCompleted logs preceded it — consistent with the runtime emitting frames at default log level (INFO) that simply do not log each message, OR the runtime producing a FinalOutput with empty response + default TokenUsage.

LIKELY PATH (ranked):
1. [HIGH] turn.rs:647-652 constructs FinalOutput.response by calling think_result.response.get('content').and_then(|c| c.as_str()).unwrap_or('').to_string(). If llm_client returns ChatMessage { content: None, tool_calls: None, .. } (LM Studio qwen3 bug where the model returns an assistant message with null content and no tool calls — seen in practice when the model 'thinks' itself into a no-op), react() produces FinalOutput { response: '' } and tokens.total=0. The stdio loop (stdio.rs:148-162) still emits StreamingDelta{delta:''} and TurnCompleted with the default TokenUsage. send_turn (sera.rs:278-344) happily accumulates an empty string and returns Ok(TurnEvents{response:'',…}). Matches all observed fields exactly.
2. [LOW] LLM HTTP-level error that returns content=None with status 200. prompt_tokens=0 rules out a normal successful call — usage.prompt_tokens.unwrap_or_default() is 0 only when the server omitted usage OR when the request never hit the LLM. But classify_http_error would bail with LlmError, producing 'turn_error' NDJSON and the 'Runtime harness turn failed' path with a non-empty '[sera] Runtime error' reply — so this is RULED OUT by the empty reply.
3. [LOW] Doom-loop Interruption — stdio.rs:196 emits '[interrupted: …]' which is always non-empty. RULED OUT.

KEY CODE POINTS:
- turn.rs:647-652 — empty-response construction when content=None
- llm_client.rs:451 — content: choice.message.content (Option<String> forwarded unchanged)
- stdio.rs:148-162 — FinalOutput emits StreamingDelta{delta:response} unconditionally, no guard for empty
- sera.rs:1202 — gateway empty-reply 502 guard (working as intended)

FIX SCOPE:
A) Runtime-side, leaf fix: in default_runtime.rs where FinalOutput is returned (or in turn.rs:647) substitute empty response with a sentinel like '[empty assistant response]' OR have llm_client mark choice.message.content=None+no tool_calls as a RequestError so Err bubbles up with a non-empty gateway reply. Pick one: prefer llm_client guard — cheap, explicit, surfaces the root cause.
B) Gateway-side (sera.rs:1202): already guards the user-visible 502. Working correctly.

THIS BUG IS THE LEAF. The gateway behaviour at sera-xk8d cascades from a slightly different root (execute_steer has no timeout; see sera-xk8d notes).

NO LIVE REPRO IN SESSION — 3 back-to-back chats all returned 200 OK with correct responses (purple/pong). The 05:00:14 event is historical. Repro is intermittent and likely depends on conversation state driving the model to emit content:null. Suggest adding a synthetic test that injects an 'Ok(LlmChatResult { message: { content: None, tool_calls: None }})' via mock LLM provider and assert runtime returns a sentinel reply, not empty.

title: sera-cli: token store always uses in-memory mock on Linux/WSL2 — auth login does not persist across invocations
description:
## Bug

`sera auth login` reports success but all subsequent commands (`agent list`, `auth whoami`, `chat`) fail with "not authenticated".

## Root cause

`Cargo.toml` declares the `keyring` crate with only `["apple-native", "windows-native"]` features. On Linux/WSL2 this compiles in the keyring mock backend (`MockCredential`), which is purely in-memory. Each process invocation creates a fresh `MockCredential { secret: None }`.

The `best_available_store()` probe calls `ks.load()` — the mock returns `Ok(None)` (not an error), so the probe passes and `KeyringTokenStore` is selected. But since the mock is in-process and non-persistent, the token saved by `auth login` is lost the moment the process exits.

The file store fallback (`~/.sera/token`) is never reached.

## Reproducer

```
# On WSL2 / Linux
sera auth login --endpoint http://localhost:3001 --token $KEY   # prints "Logged in as: autonomous"
sera agent list --endpoint http://localhost:3001                  # Error: not authenticated
```

Confirmed with `--verbose`: all store constructions log `using OS keyring` with `MockCredential { secret: None }`.

## Fix

Add `linux-secret-service` (requires Secret Service daemon) **or** add `linux-no-secret-service` / `sync-secret-service` feature to use the file-based fallback on Linux. Simplest safe fix:

```toml
# rust/Cargo.toml
keyring = { version = "3", features = ["apple-native", "windows-native", "linux-no-secret-service"] }
```

Alternatively, fix `best_available_store()` to detect the mock by attempting a write+read round-trip and falling back to `FileTokenStore` if the value doesn't survive.

## Impact

All auth-gated CLI commands are broken on Linux/WSL2: `agent list`, `agent show`, `agent run`, `auth whoami`, `chat`.

title: Discord Gateway: WebSocket protocol error on 2026-04-24T01:44:29
description: Container rust-sera-1 experienced a WebSocket protocol error (Connection reset without closing handshake) at 2026-04-24T01:44:29.424267Z. Service recovered and reconnected successfully at 01:44:34. Error is transient but indicates potential Discord Gateway timeout or network stability issue. Reproduce: monitor Discord connector logs over extended period (>24h) for frequency of such errors.
notes:
INVESTIGATION (2026-04-24):

Root cause: Discord's server-side WebSocket tear-down without a proper closing handshake. The error string 'WebSocket protocol error: Connection reset without closing handshake' is emitted by tokio-tungstenite when Discord's load balancer drops the TCP connection abruptly (no WS Close frame). This is a well-documented, expected Discord Gateway behaviour — Discord deliberately disconnects sessions on a rolling basis and expects clients to reconnect.

Frequency: 3 occurrences observed in the 4-hour log window (01:44:29, 03:00:23 as WARN/Close-frame path, 04:55:27, 05:02:44). Two events produce the ERROR path (connection reset), one produces the WARN path (Close frame received). All three recovered within 5-7 seconds.

Reconnect logic assessment: The logic in rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/discord.rs is sound. The run() loop catches the error, logs it, sleeps an interruptible 5-second backoff (polling shutting_down every 100ms), then reconnects. Heartbeat is re-established on each reconnect (41250ms interval confirmed each time). Shutdown flag integration is tested by two async unit tests. There is no exponential backoff — the delay is fixed at 5 seconds — but Discord's own reconnect guidance is to reconnect promptly (not with long backoff), so this is correct behaviour for Gateway disconnects.

No message loss: The reconnects are clean — bot is ready within ~1s of reconnecting each time. No missed MESSAGE_CREATE events are evidenced in surrounding logs.

Latent concern (minor): The heartbeat task is spawned with tokio::spawn and holds only an mpsc::Sender; if the send fails it breaks silently. There is no heartbeat-miss detection (no Heartbeat ACK timeout tracking). Discord can also send opcode 1 (server-initiated heartbeat request) which the current code ignores (falls through to the debug unhandled opcode branch). Neither gap caused the observed disconnects, but both are worth noting as future hardening candidates.

Recommended action: TIER 1 — no fix required. The disconnects are Discord-initiated, the reconnect is working correctly, and message delivery is unaffected. The only actionable improvement would be demoting the ERROR log to WARN (since this is expected protocol behaviour, not a bug) and adding a structured field like disconnect_reason=connection_reset, but that is cosmetic log hygiene, not a correctness fix.
close_reason: transient log noise; no fix needed (see notes)
