title: [bug] Turn timeout 120s is too short for thinking/local models (user-reported 2026-04-23)
description:
User report: 'Runtime harness turn timed out; releasing lane session_key=discord:sera:1482493880841670859 timeout_secs=120'

120s default is fine for cheap fast models but fails on:
- Cloud thinking models (Opus, Sonnet extended thinking): 2–10 min typical
- Local models (qwen3.6-35b, gemma-4-26b via LM Studio): 1–5 min per turn on modest hardware
- Any agentic reasoning that does multiple tool calls

Current code: rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs turn_timeout() helper. Override exists via SERA_TURN_TIMEOUT_SECS but 120s default means users hit this bug before they learn the env var exists.

## Fix

1. Raise the default from 120s to **600s** (10 minutes). That is still short enough to surface truly hung runtimes but accommodates typical thinking/local usage.
2. Allow per-agent override via Agent manifest: 'spec.turn_timeout_secs: 900' (optional). Fallback order: manifest > env var > default.
3. Log the effective timeout at turn start at info level so operators can audit what's in play.

## Out of scope
The 'fail-open' pattern around timeout (silently falls through) — that's sera-3rmo's territory.

Priority: P2. Trivial change, big UX win.

title: [bug] /api/chat returns 200 OK with empty response when execute_turn produces empty reply (silent failure)
description:
Reported by sibling agent 2026-04-23 on deployed Docker container. Observed: POST /api/chat returns 200 OK but 'response' field is empty string. Discord path works fine (same execute_turn, different caller).

Code smell at rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:1178:

    Ok(Json(ChatResponse {
        response: result.reply,  // could be empty string
        session_id,
        usage: result.usage,
    }).into_response())

The only path in execute_turn that produces empty reply is Ok(Ok(events)) where events.response is empty. Both Err paths produce '[sera] Runtime error: ...' or '[sera] Runtime timed out ...' — never empty. So empty reply == harness returned success with nothing.

This is a silent failure pattern: gateway forwards the emptiness as HTTP 200 without logging or erroring. Should instead:
- Log at error level if reply.is_empty()
- Return 502 Bad Gateway (harness returned empty) OR include error indicator in response

Note: does NOT reproduce locally with sera-local + LM Studio. Environment-specific on the deployed container — but the silent-failure masking makes the root cause (why is harness returning empty?) invisible to operators.

Priority: P2. Silent failure first, then chase the empty-harness-response root cause on the deployed container.

title: sera-gateway: decide fail-open vs fail-closed semantics for SessionStore emission (post sera-r1g8)

Decision needed: either (a) accept the trade-off and document it prominently (availability > durability under backing-store failure), or (b) change to fail-closed — route returns 5xx when emission fails, operators diagnose the store problem.

title: SPEC-plugins amendment: stdio transport + ContextEngine capability + Python/TS SDK scope
description:
Design-only bead (no code). Parent: sera-xx48.

Amend docs/plan/specs/SPEC-plugins.md (currently Status: DRAFT) with the extension-model decisions from the 2026-04-21 design pass:

1. Add STDIO transport tier alongside gRPC. Same PluginCapability enum, same Kind: Plugin manifest, new 'transport:' field (stdio | grpc). Neither transport is dev-only — per durable principle 'code vs ops is a hard line' (memory: feedback_code_vs_ops.md), the choice is an ops/deployment concern, not a code/spec gate. Operators pick IPC; sera doesn't care.

2. Add ContextEngine to PluginCapability enum. First consumer = Python LCM (hermes-agent/plugins/context_engine/lcm, ~250KB Python, 53K engine.py) wrapped via the forthcoming Python SDK. SPEC-context-engine-pluggability §8 explicitly defers trait-crate extraction until a second ContextEngine impl lands — this amendment makes the second impl viable as a plugin.

3. Scope first-class SDKs in two languages: sera-plugin-sdk-py + sera-plugin-sdk-ts. Both work over BOTH transports. Agent-friendly / ecosystem-opening is the stated motivation. Proto stays canonical; JSON Schema mirrors ship alongside (hand-written, adjacent to each .proto — no codegen pipeline).

4. Uniform security: mTLS for gRPC, socket perms for stdio. Required in the spec, operator-satisfied differently. No tier gate.

5. Uniform supervision: restart-with-backoff + heartbeat + circuit-breaker, same model for both transports.

6. Prior art note: SPEC-hooks §2.6 already specifies 'Subprocess Hooks (Language-Agnostic Extension)'. The amendment should explicitly cross-reference the subprocess/stdio pattern used there and align supervision + heartbeat semantics to whatever §2.6 established, rather than inventing a second flavor.

7. WASM hooks stay untouched. Cross-ref SPEC-plugins §1 (three distinct extension points) — unchanged. sera-s4b1 proceeds independently.

8. Cross-references to update: SPEC-memory-pluggability (sibling pluggability pattern), SPEC-context-engine-pluggability (first ContextEngine plugin consumer), SPEC-hooks (distinct surface, but share subprocess pattern), SPEC-config (Kind: Plugin manifest schema).

Out of scope: any SDK code, any plugin implementations. Spec amendment only.

title: Phase 1: sera-gateway route wrapping to Submission envelope emitters
description: Split from sera-y9d0. Most gateway routes currently call services directly, bypassing the Submission envelope. This bead wraps every agent-facing route in a Submission emitter so every observable action is mediated through the envelope (and therefore auditable + replayable by the two-layer persistence from its sibling bead). Blocks M2 full Phase 0 spec coverage. Parent: sera-y9d0.
notes:
Implementation complete — PR #1007 (https://github.com/TKCen/sera/pull/1007). mergeable=MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED only because validate-rust + ci-e2e-smoke are still in progress — will clear naturally. Bead stays in_progress until user merges.

## Delivered
- rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/session_store.rs — STUB SessionStore trait + InMemorySessionStore (pending sera-r9ed's real impl)
- AppState (both routes-level and binary-level) wired with Arc<dyn SessionStore>
- Envelope emission added to: POST /api/chat (binary + library), POST /api/agents/:id/tasks, POST /api/agents/:id/tasks/:taskId/result, POST /api/permission-requests, POST /api/intercom/publish, POST /api/intercom/dm
- 260 tests pass (4 new route-shape units + 1 integration sequence)

## COORDINATION CONFLICT WITH sera-r9ed (PR #1006) — merge order matters
Both PRs create rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/session_store.rs with DIFFERENT content:
- #1006 (r9ed): real SessionStore trait + SqliteGitSessionStore impl + 9 unit tests + 4 integration tests
- #1007 (r1g8): stub SessionStore trait + InMemorySessionStore stub + 3 unit tests

**Resolution path (documented in this bead AND in the r1g8 PR body):**
1. Merge #1006 first. r9ed's real trait + SqliteGitSessionStore land in main.
2. #1007 rebases. Expected conflicts in session_store.rs:
   - DELETE r1g8's duplicate SessionStore trait — use r9ed's
   - KEEP r1g8's InMemorySessionStore (still useful for tests, but may need minor signature tweaks to match r9ed's trait)
   - KEEP all route wiring + envelope emission — that's r1g8's substantive work
3. CI re-runs on rebase. Merge #1007.

## Concerns flagged for review before merge

1. **All wrapped routes use Op::UserTurn.** Tasks, permission-requests, intercom dm/publish are NOT semantically user turns — they're task operations, permission events, peer-agent messages. Using UserTurn for all of them breaks replay semantics (a task-result arrival will look like a user message in the audit log). The executor documented this in handler comments but did not file follow-ups. **Decision needed:** either add dedicated Op variants (Op::Task, Op::TaskResult, Op::PermissionRequest, Op::AgentDm, Op::IntercomPublish) and re-wrap, OR accept the lossy audit trail for MVS. Flagging as follow-up bead below.

2. **Store errors fail-open (logged, never reject the request).** This is a durability-vs-availability trade-off. If the PartTable+git backing store is unreachable, routes succeed but produce no audit trail — silently. SPEC-gateway should be consulted on whether this matches the intended guarantee. If the envelope is claimed to be 'auditable + replayable', fail-open violates that claim. Flagging as follow-up.

title: Phase 1: sera-gateway two-layer session persistence (PartTable + shadow git)
description: Split from sera-y9d0. Per SPEC-gateway: PartTable (primary, SQLite) holds current session state, shadow git repo persists audit-grade replay history. Every submission+emission snapshots to git as an append-only commit; PartTable holds the head reference. Goal: deterministic session replay from git + byte-for-byte auditability. Parent: sera-y9d0.
notes:
Implementation complete — PR #1006 (https://github.com/TKCen/sera/pull/1006). 6/6 CI checks green, mergeStateStatus=CLEAN. Bead stays in_progress until user merges.

## Delivered
- rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/session_store.rs — SessionStore trait + SqliteGitSessionStore impl + SubmissionRef + StoredSubmission + SessionStoreError. 9 unit tests.
- rust/crates/sera-gateway/tests/session_store_integration.rs — 4 integration tests (full submit/commit/replay cycle, reopen-from-sha, 24-writer concurrent race, shadow-repo tree shape).
- Workspace: git2 0.19 with default-features=false (no libssh2/openssl-sys dep on Linux build host).
- 429 tests pass (sera-gateway + sera-db); clippy clean; workspace check clean.

## Spec decisions executor made (on the record)
1. SessionStore trait kept to 3 methods the bead called out — no speculative additions. GOOD.
2. Commit layout: submission.json at tree root + emissions/<0000>.json blobs in emissions/ subtree; one commit per append_submission.
3. Determinism: fixed signature + fixed epoch (1767225600 = 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z); replay SHA survives reopen byte-for-byte.
4. Atomicity: tokio Mutex<Connection> + BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction flips git HEAD + session_heads UPSERT together.
5. Reused sera_types::envelope::Submission as the canonical envelope type; store takes &StoredSubmission { submission, emissions } — no new wrapper.
6. Left legacy session_persist.rs P0 PartTable/SessionSnapshot stubs untouched (unused elsewhere; follow-up bead can delete after audit shows no callers).

## Concern flagged (Simplicity First — review before merge)
- HeadConflict error variant declared but UNREACHABLE under the current mutex strategy. Executor kept it as 'forward-compatible public API affordance for a future optimistic-locking switch'. This is the kind of speculative flexibility Simplicity First explicitly forbids ('No flexibility or configurability that wasn't requested'). Recommend: delete the variant, add it back when optimistic locking is actually being implemented. Low stakes (enum variant), but violates the project principle.

## Coordination with sera-r1g8 (running in parallel)
Per the executor prompts, sera-r1g8 was told to use SessionStore if it exists in main, else define a minimal stub. Since r9ed was in-flight when r1g8 fired, r1g8 will have defined its own stub trait. Expected resolution: r9ed merges first, r1g8 rebases and swaps its stub for this real trait. No blocking issue; natural rebase path.

title: Phase 1: sera-memory crate — SemanticMemoryStore trait + BM25 + pgvector adapter
description: Currently memory lives in sera-session with 4 tiers (hot/warm/cold/archived). Per SPEC-memory and user preference: we need a dedicated 'sera-memory' crate exposing a SemanticMemoryStore trait with: (a) SQLite FTS5 default tier (local-first), (b) pgvector enterprise tier, (c) mem0 / hindsight / RAG as plugins. Blocked by Phase 0 workflow engine persistence (Lane H). Must not require Postgres locally.
notes:
## Resolved design — 2026-04-20

**Trait revision (breaking change, single PR with crate extract):**
- New `PutRequest { agent_id, content, scope, tier, tags, promoted, supplied_embedding: Option<Vec<f32>> }` as the write input.
- `SemanticEntry.embedding: Vec<f32>` → `Option<Vec<f32>>`. Hindsight-style backends return None; pgvector returns Some.
- `SemanticMemoryStore::put` signature becomes `async fn put(&self, req: PutRequest) -> Result<MemoryId, SemanticError>`.
- Backends decide: if supplied_embedding is None, backend embeds via its own EmbeddingService (pgvector path) or server-side (hindsight path). If Some, backend trusts caller.
- Existing call sites in sera-runtime (tools/memory_search.rs), sera-workflow (memory_manager.rs, semantic_eviction.rs, sleeptime.rs), sera-session (indexer.rs), sera-plugins (registry.rs) update in the same PR.

**Crate extraction:**
- Move SemanticMemoryStore + Scope/Damping/ScopeHierarchy/MemoryHit/MemoryId/SemanticEntry/SemanticQuery/ScoredEntry/EvictionPolicy/SemanticStats/SemanticError from `sera-types::semantic_memory` into new `sera-memory` crate.
- Move PgVectorStore + SqliteMemoryStore from sera-db into sera-memory.
- Move InMemorySemanticStore from sera-testing into sera-memory (or keep in testing behind a feature — executor picks).
- sera-types re-exports for back-compat during migration (remove in follow-up bead).

**Design doc:**
- New `docs/plan/specs/SPEC-memory-pluggability.md` with hindsight + LCM worked as shape-proofs. Conformance by construction, no adapter code.

**Out of scope (separate beads):**
- Real hindsight adapter → sera-fnaj (plugin crate).
- ContextEngine pluggability where LCM fits → sera-ze27 (reframed).
- LCM backend port → Phase 4 per SPEC-memory §3.2, amended by sera-lg2i.

**Conformance rules (bake into the crate's README):**
1. Backend MAY own embeddings (caller passes content, not a vector).
2. Backend MAY choose async latency (no sync-only assumption in trait).
3. Backend MAY reject in-place update (hindsight has no per-memory update).
4. Backend MAY reject per-id delete (hindsight bulk-deletes by type).
5. Backend MUST filter by agent_id + optional Scope.
6. Backend MUST return SemanticError for network/storage faults — no silent zero-vectors.

title: Local embedding provider: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 on CPU via fastembed-rs or candle (zero external service)
description:
Ship an embedding provider that runs entirely on the local CPU — no Ollama required, no OpenAI key, no remote API. Pairs with the basic SQLite memory tier (sera-vzce) to close the zero-infrastructure RAG story.

### Model choice

Default: 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2' (384 dims, sentence-transformers MIT license, ~80MB ONNX weights). Battle-tested in the fastembed / Hermes / OpenClaw ecosystems. Fast enough on a single CPU core for interactive use.

### Runtime options (pick ONE based on binary-size + portability tradeoffs)

- **Option A — fastembed-rs:** Rust port of fastembed, uses ONNX Runtime. Preferred if binary size and model-caching story are acceptable. Handles tokenisation + inference end-to-end.
- **Option B — candle (HuggingFace):** Pure-Rust tensor library. Heavier code surface but no ONNX dep. Good if we want minimal runtime deps.
- **Option C — ORT bindings directly:** Max control, max complexity.

Decision recorded in the bead's design notes once an ADR lands.

### Files

- new 'rust/crates/sera-runtime/src/semantic/providers/local.rs' — 'LocalEmbeddingService' impl
- model caching: download on first use to '~/.cache/sera/models/<model-id>/' with an integrity check (sha256). Offline-resumable.
- impl sera_types::EmbeddingService:
  - model_id() → 'sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'
  - dimensions() → 384
  - embed(&texts) → tokenise + forward pass, normalise to unit length, return Vec<Vec<f32>>
  - health() → quick self-test against a single token
- Config: 'SERA_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=local' (alongside existing 'ollama' and 'openai'); default for pure-local profile.

### Acceptance

- 'cargo test -p sera-runtime --features local-embedding' covers: embed single text, batch embed 32 texts, dimension correctness, deterministic output given same input.
- First run downloads the model; subsequent runs load from cache in <200ms.
- p50 embed latency for a single short sentence: <50ms on a modern laptop (no GPU).
- Embeddings match the reference all-MiniLM-L6-v2 output within f32 tolerance (sanity-check against fastembed Python).
- Feature-gated so users who prefer Ollama/OpenAI embeddings pay zero binary-size cost.

Deps: sera-vzce consumes this for its vector side. Can land independently — sera-vzce degrades to BM25-only without it. ~3-4 days depending on runtime choice.

title: Memory plugin architecture: document SemanticMemoryStore as the user-pluggable memory seam (mem0, hindsight, RAG, ...)
description:
SERA's memory is pluggable. Users who outgrow the basic SQLite-FTS tier can plug in RAG systems, mem0, hindsight, or any custom backend by implementing sera_types::SemanticMemoryStore. This bead formalises and documents the plugin contract.

Scope:
1. docs/ARCHITECTURE — new 'Memory tiers' section:
   - Tier-0: MemoryBlock (in-process, always on)
   - Tier-1: SemanticMemoryStore (pluggable)
     - Basic: SqliteFtsMemoryStore (sera-vzce — zero-dep keyword search)
     - Enterprise: PgVectorStore (Postgres + pgvector, dense-vector recall)
     - Plugin: user-supplied impl (mem0, hindsight, external RAG service, …)
   - Tier-2: ContextEnricher auto-promotes hits into MemoryBlock on each turn.
2. docs/plugins/memory.md — the user-facing contract:
   - Trait signature, error policy (fail loudly, no silent fallbacks), agent_id isolation, dedupe via MemoryId.
   - Example skeleton plugin crate (e.g. sera-memory-mem0 stub) showing how to wire a user impl into the gateway via config.
3. Gateway config: allow 'memory.backend: sqlite-fts | pgvector | plugin:<path-or-name>' in sera.yaml. Plugin mode loads a dynlib or a named crate via cargo features.
4. Optional: reference-impl stubs (feature-gated) for mem0 HTTP adapter and hindsight adapter to make the plugin surface concrete.

Acceptance:
- docs describe the four memory tiers clearly, mark which are built-in vs optional.
- sera.yaml accepts 'memory.backend' and routes gateway to the chosen impl.
- At least one end-to-end test exercises the 'plugin:' path with a mock user-impl.

title: sera-cli streaming: Centrifugo WS or gateway SSE for 'sera agent run'
description:
Centrifugo is OPTIONAL infrastructure for enterprise/multi-pod scalability — a pure local setup should NOT require it. Gateway stream:true mode currently publishes tokens to a Centrifugo channel 'tokens:{agentId}'; sera-cli falls back to stream:false for a single-shot reply. For a real interactive 'sera chat':

Decide between three paths (local-first):
(a) HTTP SSE on the gateway — gateway streams tokens directly over the /api/chat response (text/event-stream). No Centrifugo required. Preferred for local.
(b) Gateway SSE proxy that bridges Centrifugo when it's configured — degrades to (a) when Centrifugo is absent.
(c) Centrifugo WS in the CLI — enterprise-only; adds client complexity and a hard dep.

Implementation should keep Centrifugo as a pluggable enhancement, not a requirement. sera agent run must work over plain HTTP in the local profile.

title: Better handling of 429 rate-limit errors from upstream providers
description:
## Problem
When an upstream provider returns 429 (rate limited), the error surfaces as a generic stream error:
```
[LLMProxy] LLM stream error | agent=...: 429 Provider returned error
qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free is temporarily rate-limited upstream
```

Current behavior:
- The error is logged but not distinguished from other stream errors
- No automatic retry with backoff before failing
- No failover to an alternative model
- No surfacing of retry-after headers to the agent/UI
- The agent-runtime retries blindly (MAX_PROVIDER_RETRIES=1) without knowing it's a rate limit

## Expected behavior
1. **Detect 429 specifically** in LlmRouter/llmProxy streaming path
2. **Extract retry-after** header if present and wait before retrying
3. **Trigger failover** to failoverModels chain (PR #860) on rate limit
4. **Surface rate limit info** in the error response (provider, retry-after, suggestion)
5. **Track rate limit events** per provider/model for the dynamic routing system (sera-48j)

## Related
- sera-48j: Dynamic model & provider routing (will use rate limit tracking data)
- PR #860: failoverModels chain (should auto-trigger on 429)
- PR #869: Streaming metering (stream error path)

## Files likely involved
- `core/src/llm/LlmRouter.ts` — dispatch error handling
- `core/src/routes/llmProxy.ts` — streaming error response
- `core/src/llm/CircuitBreakerService.ts` — should count 429s differently from 5xx

title: CLI/TUI client consolidation — Rust rewrite
description:
The project has two separate terminal clients that need consolidation:

## Current State
- **cli/** — Go-based CLI (minimal, uses go.mod)
- **tui/** — Go-based TUI with WebSocket connection to Centrifugo (main.go + ws.go)
- Both are Go, both talk to sera-core, overlapping functionality

## Proposed: Consolidate into a single Rust CLI/TUI

### Why Rust
- Aligns with the sera-core-rs strangler fig work (shared types, API client)
- Better async story (tokio) for WebSocket + HTTP multiplexing
- ratatui ecosystem is mature for TUI (better than bubbletea equivalents)
- Single binary distribution, cross-platform
- Can share the Rust API client with sera-core-rs

### Features for the consolidated client
1. **Chat mode** — interactive chat with sera (streaming responses via Centrifugo)
2. **Task management** — create/list/check orchestration tasks from terminal
3. **Bridge control** — start/stop/status of bridge agents
4. **Model browser** — list available models from all providers (uses ModelDiscoveryService)
5. **Metrics dashboard** — TUI view of orchestration metrics (sparklines, tables)
6. **Schedule management** — create/edit cron schedules
7. **Agent management** — list/start/stop agents
8. **Log viewer** — tail sera-core logs with filtering

### Tech Stack
- **ratatui** for TUI rendering
- **clap** for CLI argument parsing
- **reqwest** for HTTP client (sera-core API)
- **tokio-tungstenite** for Centrifugo WebSocket
- **serde** for JSON serialization

### Migration Path
1. Build Rust CLI/TUI as sera-cli in a new crate
2. Add to rust/Cargo.toml workspace
3. Deprecate cli/ and tui/ Go directories
4. Keep Go versions working until Rust version reaches feature parity

title: Web UI comprehensive UX redesign — dynamic views + orchestration control
description:
The web UI needs a comprehensive UX design pass to support the orchestration capabilities and provide superior control/insights.

## Current State
- Basic pages for agents, channels, schedules, chat, memory, etc.
- New orchestration dashboard added (Phase 2) but minimal
- No dynamic component loading (everything loads upfront)
- No unified design language for data-heavy views

## Needed
1. **Orchestration control center** — real-time bridge status, task queue visualization, routing rule management, metrics dashboards with charts/trends
2. **Dynamic view loading** — lazy-load pages and components to keep initial bundle small; ties into sera-6h1 gated skills concept for the backend
3. **Agent configuration UX** — model picker populated from ModelDiscoveryService, provider health indicators, cost estimation
4. **Task timeline view** — Gantt-style or timeline visualization of orchestration tasks across bridges
5. **Notification center** — unified view of ChannelRouter events, filterable by type/severity
6. **Memory/knowledge explorer** — graph visualization of sera's knowledge, search, dedup insights
7. **Schedule management** — cron expression builder, orchestration task templates, execution history
8. **Dark mode refinement** — the Aurora Cyber theme needs polish for data-dense views
9. **Mobile responsive** — at minimum the chat and notification views

## Tech Considerations
- Consider React Server Components or route-based code splitting
- TanStack Query already handles caching; add optimistic updates for mutations
- Centrifugo real-time already wired; expand to all data-changing views
- Accessibility pass (keyboard navigation, screen reader support)
design: COMPREHENSIVE REDESIGN PLAN READY. Consolidate 24 pages to 11 routes. Three-tier thought display (badge/key-events/full). Cmd+K command palette. Merge observability pages into /observe. Absorb admin pages into /settings. Agent detail: 3 tabs with sub-nav. Dashboard: health alerts + running agents + recent errors. Phase 1 (chat UX fix): 3-5 days. Phase 2 (nav consolidation): 5-8 days. Phase 3 (dashboard+polish): 5-7 days. Full plan in design agent output.

Pain points: (1) thought display spammy + defaults to expanded, (2) no thought granularity (only global on/off), (3) dual sidebar in chat eats 316px, (4) 15 agent detail tabs stacked 7-deep per meta-tab, (5) providers/mcp-servers are dead code, (6) Health/Schedules/Tools hidden from nav, (7) no Cmd+K. Quick wins: remove dead pages, add Health to sidebar, thought summary mode. Full audit + redesign plan in design agent outputs.

title: Dynamic model listing from cloud providers
description:
Providers (OpenRouter, Google AI Studio, Kilo Code) should dynamically fetch and expose available models so users can browse and select models in the web UI without hardcoding each one in providers.json.

## Provider Model Endpoints

**OpenRouter:** GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models
- Free model router: openrouter/free (auto-selects best free model)
- Free models include: Qwen 3.6 Plus, Lyria 3 Pro, Nemotron-3 Super 120B, Step 3.5 Flash, Gemma 3 12B, Mistral Small 3.1
- Rate limits: 50 req/day (free), 1000 req/day (with $10 credits)

**Google AI Studio:** GET https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models?key=API_KEY
- Latest models: gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview

**Kilo Code:** Gateway at https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway (OpenAI-compatible)
- Free Kilo Gateway models: MiniMax M2.1, GLM 4.7, Kimi K2.5, Giga Potato, Arcee Trinity Large Preview
- Free OpenRouter tier: Qwen3 Coder, GLM 4.5 Air, DeepSeek R1 0528, Kimi K2
- Budget models: Mistral Devstral Small (~$0.20/M), Llama 4 Maverick (~$0.30/M), DeepSeek v3 (~$0.27/M), Qwen3 235B (~$1.20/M)
- Uses standard model IDs (e.g. gpt-4o, claude-sonnet-4-20250514)
- Needs investigation: model listing endpoint

## Implementation

1. Add a ModelDiscoveryService that queries each provider's /models endpoint
2. Cache results (refresh every hour or on demand)
3. Expose via GET /api/providers/:provider/models
4. Web UI: model picker dropdown in agent config populated from discovery
5. Allow filtering by: free/paid, context window, capabilities (vision, tools, reasoning)

title: [performance] sera-gateway/discord: bot_user_id uses std::sync::Mutex inside async handlers — risk of blocking the runtime executor under contention
description: rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/discord.rs:39 declares 'bot_user_id: std::sync::Mutex<Option<String>>' and locks it inside the async handle_payload (line 366, 379). std::sync::Mutex::lock() is a synchronous, blocking primitive — under tokio it stalls the executor thread for the duration of the lock. Today the critical sections are short (one read, one optional write) and contention is minimal because the WebSocket reader is single-threaded, but: (a) future per-event tasks may take this lock concurrently, (b) clippy::await_holding_lock would flag any future code that holds it across .await, (c) the project uses tokio::sync::RwLock pervasively elsewhere (state.lane_queue, state.capability_registry).\n\nThis is preemptive cleanup: cheap to fix now, expensive to fix once the connector is split into multi-task message dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Replace std::sync::Mutex<Option<String>> with tokio::sync::RwLock<Option<String>> (or std::sync::OnceLock if write-once semantics fit — bot_user_id is set once on READY). 2) Adjust lock sites to .read().await / .write().await. 3) cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings stays clean. 4) Note in module-level doc that bot_user_id is single-write.

Several existing beads describe specific route gaps (sera-cmoy /api/auth/login + logout, sera-iogn MCP bridge, sera-nffd /v1/chat/completions, sera-sa6r /api/agents POST/DELETE) — but there is no single pass that diffs the current router(s) against the spec, so new divergences are noticed only when a downstream client breaks.\n\nReproduction: grep '.route(' rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs | wc -l vs grep '^paths:' -A 99999 docs/openapi.yaml | grep '^[[:space:]]/' | wc -l — the counts will not match.

The current sera-gateway code calls the latter StdioHarness even though only InProcess transport is wired. Add a glossary section that names two integration patterns explicitly: Pattern A (BYOH harness-as-runtime, e.g. Hermes ACP, sera-byoh-agent — turn-bounded, registers tools through gateway dispatch) vs Pattern B (profile-as-subagent ExternalAgentPrincipal, e.g. Claude Code tmux pane, OMC orchestrator — session-bounded, opaque internal loop). Should also document the §3.1 compaction-invisibility tradeoff for Pattern B.
design: Documentation only — no code change in this bead. The taxonomy is the prerequisite for sera-5mbr/w2dh/eq0m/kg3g/pcvp landing without naming-collision rework.
acceptance_criteria: Spec diff (in docs/plan/specs/SPEC-gateway.md or a new SPEC-harness.md) defines both patterns and references each existing trait without renaming any of them. Spec mentions: (a) when to use which pattern, (b) the state-ownership table from report §2, (c) the Pattern B compaction-invisibility tradeoff. Reviewed by a second author.
notes:
References: SPEC-gateway §7.0 + §7a, SPEC-runtime §2.2, ARCHITECTURE-2.0 §6a (DelegationBus = Pattern B kernel), report §1 / §2 / §3.1 / §5 B1+B10.

Checked lines 89-151: glossary anchor sera-9wce defines Pattern A harness-as-runtime using AgentRuntime/SPEC-runtime §2.2; Pattern B profile-as-subagent using ExternalAgentPrincipal/delegating principal; when-to-use table; state-ownership table; and Pattern B compaction-invisibility tradeoff. title: [coverage-gap] sera-gateway/discord: no fuzzy/malformed-payload tests for parse_message_create + handle_payload
description: rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/discord.rs has 'safe' tests for well-formed payloads (test_parse_message_create_valid, test_parse_heartbeat_interval_wrong_opcode, etc) but no negative tests for: (1) MESSAGE_CREATE with missing 'content' (returns None silently), (2) MESSAGE_CREATE where author is missing, (3) op:0 with t:'TYPING_START' or other unhandled events, (4) payloads where 'op' is a string instead of u64, (5) deeply nested or unicode-bomb payloads. The handle_payload function uses .unwrap_or(u64::MAX) on op and the parse_* helpers silently return None — but a hostile gateway server could craft payloads that DOS the runtime via excessive logging or large strings. None of this is exercised today.\n\nMotivation: Discord is the primary external connector. The parser sits behind a TLS WebSocket, so 'malicious' payloads are unusual — but a misbehaving gateway region or a man-in-the-middle scenario could deliver them. Cheap insurance.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Add proptest or hand-rolled tests for malformed JSON shapes — at minimum: missing required fields, wrong types on op/s/d, truncated payloads. 2) Confirm parse_* helpers never panic on any input, only return None. 3) Add a 1MB-string MESSAGE_CREATE test to verify no OOM-by-log; bound the content the connector forwards. 4) Document the threat model briefly in a module-level comment.

title: [bug] [security-p3] sera-gateway: validate_api_key uses non-constant-time comparison for Bearer token
description:
rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/bin/sera.rs:1052-1055 compares the request's Bearer token to the configured API key with the default String == String, which short-circuits at the first mismatched byte. Over a network this leaks ~nanoseconds per matched prefix byte and is generally not exploitable, but it is the kind of finding security reviewers flag and is trivial to fix with subtle::ConstantTimeEq or similar. Same pattern repeats in routes/a2a.rs:check_auth (line 91-103).

Current: 'Some(token) if token == expected => Ok(())' inside validate_api_key.
Proposed: pad to equal length and compare with constant-time helper, or use the 'subtle' crate.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Add 'subtle' crate (or equivalent) to sera-gateway and sera-a2a/routes shared deps. 2) Replace token == expected in validate_api_key + check_auth with constant-time compare. 3) Unit test asserts that two non-matching keys of equal length still return Err(401). 4) Note the pattern in rust/CLAUDE.md so it isn't reintroduced elsewhere.

title: [bug] sera-gateway/discord: fixed 5s reconnect sleep — no exponential backoff or jitter, herd risk on gateway flap
description: rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/discord.rs:215-223 sleeps a constant 5 seconds between reconnect attempts. Discord's developer guidance is to use truncated exponential backoff with jitter (e.g. min 1s, max 30s, +/- random) to avoid synchronized reconnect storms across many bots when Discord rolls out gateway changes. Coupled with the missing RESUME path (separate bead), every flap also pays a full IDENTIFY. With a single bot the practical impact is small, but it becomes a guaranteed self-DoS once multiple SERA agents share a single gateway region.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Replace fixed 5s with truncated-exponential backoff (1s base, 30s cap) plus +/-25% jitter, reset on a successful READY. 2) State machine retains attempt counter across loop iterations. 3) Unit test asserts the backoff sequence with jitter disabled (deterministic mode) for 5 consecutive failures matches expected schedule.

title: chore(web): W.2 review follow-ups
description:
Follow-ups from code review of #1108 + #1109 (Mr. Claude session 2026-04-29). Both PRs approved; these are non-blocking but worth landing before W.x adds more per-principal queries.

MEDIUM (pick up before merging W.3 chat):
1. signOut leaks server cache across users — web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:46-50. Add queryClient.clear() to signOut and to the 401 branch in validate(). Reviewer flagged this as 'the single change that will hurt most when W.3 stacks on top'.
2. getReadiness 503 body cast without validation — web/src/lib/api.ts:79-86. Either narrow with a type guard before returning, or rethrow when the shape doesn't match {status, runtime_connected}.
3. apiFetch Content-Type heuristic — web/src/lib/api.ts:31-33. Auto-setting application/json overwrites the browser's correct boundary header for FormData/URLSearchParams/Blob. Restrict auto-set to plain objects/strings.

LOW (batch when convenient):
4. ProtectedRoute drops search+hash on redirect — web/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx:18. Use full location object.
5. LoginView 'from' is unvalidated — web/src/views/LoginView.tsx:14-15. Validate it starts with a single '/' and isn't '//...'.
6. AuthMe.mode typed as 'autonomous' | string — web/src/lib/api.ts:74. Collapses to string; either narrow to closed enum or just 'string'.
7. No cross-tab sign-out. Add a window.addEventListener('storage', ...) that calls signOut() when sera.auth.token is removed elsewhere.

Parent: sera-8kvc.
notes:
MEDIUMs LANDED on W.2 branch (commit pushed 2026-04-29):
- ✓ signOut + 401-validate path now call queryClient.clear() (web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx)
- ✓ getReadiness validates 503 body shape via isReadiness type guard before returning (web/src/lib/api.ts)
- ✓ apiFetch Content-Type heuristic restricted to plain string bodies (web/src/lib/api.ts)

REMAINING (LOW, not blocking):

Verified: typecheck, lint, build green. Pushed to feat/web-auth-dashboard-sera-oi4d, propagates to PR #1109.

title: bug(sera-runtime): gate_true_for_value_one flakes under parallel test execution
description: The 4 unit tests for resolve_allow_missing_gate() in sera-runtime/src/main.rs (around line 492) all read+mutate the same SERA_ALLOW_MISSING_CONSTITUTIONAL_GATE env var. When cargo test runs them in parallel, one races and asserts on a stale value. Symptom: 'gate_true_for_value_one' fails with 'assertion failed: resolve_allow_missing_gate()'. Reproduces ~10% under cargo test --workspace; passes 100% in isolation. Fix: serialize the four tests via a Mutex<()> static, OR split each into a separate process via a #[test] dance, OR refactor resolve_allow_missing_gate() to take an env-source parameter so tests can inject. Cheap fix, ~30 LOC.

title: chore(sera): L.6 binary consolidation — rename ser → sera, absorb sera-cli
description: Final consolidation step. Rename binary 'ser' (in sera-gateway crate) → 'sera'. Absorb sera-cli crate's config layer + OS keychain handling into the unified sera bin. Delete sera-cli crate entirely (no deprecation, no alias — codebase not actively used). Keep sera-runtime as separate spawnable bin (gateway invokes it as NDJSON child). Update all docs, scripts/sera-local references, CI. Done when: 'cargo build' produces one 'sera' binary covering server+client+admin verbs; 'which ser' returns nothing; sera-cli crate removed from workspace; CI green. Deps: L.2, L.4.
notes: Investigation 2026-05-02: bead description references 'ser' binary that does not exist. Current state: sera-gateway produces 'sera-gateway' bin; sera-cli produces 'sera' bin; sera-runtime produces 'sera-runtime' bin. The 'sera' bin already exists (sera-cli). Real task is the consolidation: absorb sera-cli into sera-gateway's bin, rename sera-gateway bin to 'sera', delete sera-cli crate. Scope: 6258 LOC in sera-cli + scripts/docs sweep — well over the 50-file split threshold. Recommend splitting into: (a) rename sera-gateway bin to 'sera-server' as interim no-conflict step + scripts/docs sweep — small; (b) absorb sera-cli into the renamed bin, delete sera-cli crate — large and architecturally load-bearing. Lane orchestrator skipping due to context budget; recommend a fresh dedicated session.

title: feat(sera): L.5 main agent + control_plane capability
description: Privileged agent path for in-SERA self-management. New reserved policy preset capability-policies/control-plane.yaml grants admin tool allowlist. Admin tool wrappers in sera-tools (sera_admin_workflow_create, sera_admin_policy_reload, sera_admin_session_kill, etc.). Tool dispatch in sera-runtime calls L.3 admin HTTP endpoints — gateway re-checks capability + audits (single source of truth, not duplicated in runtime). 'Main agent' = any agent with policyRef: control-plane (no special code path, multiple are allowed — user decides what makes an agent main). Done when: agent with policyRef: control-plane successfully invokes sera_admin_workflow_create as a tool; agent without it gets PolicyDenial with audit log entry. Deps: L.3 + sera-eo71 (CapabilityPolicy enforcement wiring — independently filed prereq).

title: Runtime tool-registry rejects before gateway CapabilityRegistry check
description: When the LLM returns tool_calls for a tool name the runtime doesn't have in its in-process registry (per-agent), the runtime replies '[tool error: tool not found: X]' locally — before the gateway's CapabilityRegistry.check() ever fires. S4.1 scenario test discovered this: agent with tools.allow:[http_request] + policyRef:deny-all still gets 'tool not found' instead of the expected '[sera-policy] denied by capability policy'. Expected: the runtime should either (a) forward unknown-tool dispatches to the gateway so the audit trail reflects policy enforcement, OR (b) gateway should pre-filter the tool list sent to the LLM based on CapabilityRegistry+agent manifest. Filed from sera-9tim Phase 3.

title: sera CLI requires auth token even when gateway is autonomous
description: sera agent run / sera chat demand a stored bearer via best_available_store() and abort with exit code 2 + 'not authenticated' if none is found. The gateway in autonomous mode accepts any bearer (including none). This asymmetry means new users running a local gateway cannot use the CLI until they run sera auth login against a provider that doesn't actually enforce auth. Options: (a) CLI reads SERA_API_KEY env as a last-resort token; (b) CLI falls back to no Authorization header when --endpoint points at localhost; (c) bootstrap flow writes a dev token to $HOME/.sera/token. Currently test scenarios have to pre-seed the token file. Filed from sera-9tim Phase 1 S3.3.

title: sera start --local: probe URL should be env-overridable (SERA_LOCAL_LLM_URL)
description: K.0 hard-codes http://localhost:1234/v1/models for the LM Studio probe. This blocks integration tests (and any CI runner lacking LM Studio at that exact port) from exercising the --local code path. Adding SERA_LOCAL_LLM_URL (or similar) env override is a ~5-line change in apply_local_defaults that would unblock S1.3 'local-mode banner emitted' scenario.

title: chore(sera): K.2 prune or implement dead-weight stubs

title: POST /api/chat stream:true emits only 'event: done', no intermediate delta events
description: When stream:true, SSE response contains only a single 'event: done' frame with no preceding token/delta events. Actual output: 'event: done\ndata: {"status":"complete","usage":{"completion_tokens":0,"prompt_tokens":0,"total_tokens":0}}'. Expected: multiple incremental token/delta frames before done. All token counts are zero. Content-type is correctly text/event-stream. Streaming clients receive no incremental output — the stream behaves as a single-shot response. Tested with messages 'say just OK', 'say hi', 'Count to 3'.

title: [not-exposed] Agent create (POST) and delete (DELETE) not implemented on /api/agents
description: GET /api/agents returns agent list (200). GET /api/agents/{name} returns agent detail (200, tested with 'sera'). POST /api/agents and DELETE /api/agents/sera both return 405 Method Not Allowed with Allow: GET,HEAD header. Agent CRUD beyond read is not exposed. Additionally: /api/agent/list, /api/agent (root), /api/agents/sera/status all return 404 — sub-resource paths not implemented.

title: 401 Unauthorized responses have empty body (no JSON error envelope)
description: All auth-gated endpoints return HTTP 401 with content-length: 0 and no body when bearer token is missing or invalid. Evidence: curl -s -D - POST /api/chat (no auth) -> 'HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized / content-length: 0'. Same on GET /api/auth/me. Expected: structured JSON error body e.g. {"error":"unauthorized"} with content-type: application/json. Affects /api/chat and /api/auth/me at minimum.

Fix: in the hook handler that wraps ConstitutionalRegistry::evaluate, emit an AuditEntry (OCSF action=blocked, category=constitutional_gate, rule_id + proposer_scopes + artifact_ref) before returning the Err.

title: [cleanup] Smaller duplicate types — EnforcementMode, CircuitState, RuntimeError, HarnessError, ToolError, ConnectorError, KillSwitchError, SessionRow, AuditRow, ManifestMetadata, AgentSpec, PluginRegistration, ConstitutionalRule, AgentCapability, PingCommand, WorkflowMemoryManager, WorkingMemoryTier, MemoryStats, MemoryId, Session, Task, ChangeArtifactId, TurnContext, ChatMessage
description:
From dup audit 2026-04-23 (evening). Batch umbrella for all 2x-only duplicates found. Each pair below is a real duplicate with divergent shapes; pick one owner and collapse.

Canonical candidates in parentheses:

1. EnforcementMode: sera-types::skill::EnforcementMode {Enforced,Advisory} vs sera-hitl::mode::EnforcementMode {Autonomous,Standard,Strict} — NOT a real duplicate (different domain), just name-colliding. Rename one.

2. CircuitState: sera-models/src/routing.rs:74 vs sera-plugins/src/circuit_breaker.rs:15 — same 3 variants (Closed/Open/HalfOpen). Canonical: sera-plugins (circuit breaker is a plugin concern).

3. RuntimeError: sera-types/src/runtime.rs:197 vs sera-runtime/src/error.rs:5 — overlapping variants. Canonical: sera-types.

4. HarnessError: sera-types/src/harness.rs:38 vs sera-runtime/src/harness.rs:81 — different variants. Canonical: sera-types.

5. ToolError: sera-types/src/tool.rs:410 vs sera-runtime/src/turn.rs:100 — overlap on NotFound/ExecutionFailed. Canonical: sera-types.

6. ConnectorError: sera-gateway/src/connector/mod.rs:21 vs sera-types/src/connector.rs:75 — types has richer variants. Canonical: sera-types.

7. KillSwitchError: sera-gateway/src/kill_switch.rs:174 vs sera-tools/src/kill_switch.rs:11 — completely different variants; genuine name collision. Pick one crate per SPEC-kill-switch.

8. SessionRow: sera-db/src/sessions.rs:8 (sqlx/PgPool) vs sera-db/src/sqlite.rs:15 (rusqlite) — intentional dual-backend (per rust/CLAUDE.md both coexist). Mark explicitly as #[cfg(feature='postgres')] vs rusqlite to remove ambiguity.

9. AuditRow: sera-db/src/audit.rs:21 (sqlx) vs sera-db/src/sqlite.rs:37 (rusqlite). Same fix as SessionRow.

10. ManifestMetadata: sera-plugins/src/manifest.rs:52 vs sera-runtime/src/manifest.rs:53 — plugins has annotations, runtime has namespace. Real drift.

11. AgentSpec: sera-types/src/config_manifest.rs:197 (flat MVS) vs sera-runtime/src/manifest.rs:63 (full nested with identity/model/tools/memory/intercom). Real shape drift.

12. PluginRegistration: sera-plugins/src/types.rs:126 (full descriptor with transport, health_check) vs sera-types/src/harness.rs:93 ({name, namespace}). The types-crate one is a stub; delete it, re-export from sera-plugins.

13. ConstitutionalRule: sera-meta/src/constitutional.rs:17 (wraps 'base' with scopes/blast_radii/required_scopes) vs sera-types/src/evolution.rs:52 (base: {id, description, enforcement_point, content_hash}). Documented in code — meta wraps the types base. Not a duplicate, just confusing naming. Rename meta one to ConstitutionalRuleEntry.

14. AgentCapability: sera-types/src/capability.rs:82 vs sera-types/src/evolution.rs:83 — IDENTICAL in same crate (5 variants each: MetaChange, CodeChange, MetaApprover, ConfigRead, ConfigPropose). One is copy-paste slop. Pick one file.

15. PingCommand: sera-commands/src/commands/ping.rs:13 (command-bus ping, returns 'pong') vs sera-cli/src/commands/ping.rs:17 (CLI subcommand, hits /api/health). Different semantics, same name — rename the CLI one to HealthCheckCommand.

16. WorkflowMemoryManager: sera-workflow/src/memory_manager.rs:117 (coordinator_scoped_summary<InstanceId, InstanceBucket>) vs sera-workflow/src/coordination.rs:362 (HashMap<String, Value>). Two WM stores in the SAME crate. One is dead-or-drift. Pick one.

17. WorkingMemoryTier: sera-session/src/memory_wrapper.rs:104 vs sera-types/src/memory.rs:190 — IDENTICAL 4-variant enums with comments noting 'matches sera_types::WorkingMemoryTier'. Delete the sera-session copy, re-export.

18. MemoryStats: sera-session/src/memory_wrapper.rs:66 ({entry_count, estimated_tokens, tier}) vs sera-types/src/memory.rs:383 ({total_entries, entries_by_tier, total_size_bytes, index_status}). Real drift — session is simpler in-memory stats; types is backend-level stats. Rename session one to WorkingMemoryStats.

19. MemoryId: sera-types/src/memory.rs:236 vs sera-memory/src/store.rs:230 — IDENTICAL pub struct MemoryId(pub String) with same constructors. Delete sera-memory copy, re-export from sera-types.

20. Session: sera-types/src/session.rs:340 vs sera-tui/src/client.rs:124 — the tui one is a flat summary (id, agent_id, created_at, state: String) built from_json. Intentional decoupling per tui/CLAUDE.md (tui only depends on reqwest/types). Rename tui one SessionSummary.

21. Task: sera-types/src/signal.rs:154 (internal dispatch {id, description, payload?}) vs sera-a2a/src/lib.rs:102 (A2A protocol {id, status, artifacts, history, metadata}). Two different protocols; not a duplicate but sharing the name inside the same workspace is fragile. Rename a2a one A2ATask.

22. ChangeArtifactId: sera-types/src/evolution.rs:6 ({hash: [u8;32]}, content-addressed) vs sera-config/src/version_log.rs:8 (String wrapper). Drift. Canonical: sera-types (evolution is the spec home).

23. TurnContext: sera-types/src/runtime.rs:21 (the SPEC-runtime data) vs sera-runtime/src/turn.rs:151 (richer with turn_id, react_mode, doom_loop_count, enforcement_mode, pending_steer, tool_context). The runtime one is the real usable one. Plan: absorb sera-types::runtime::TurnContext into sera-runtime or rename to TurnContextSpec.

24. ChatMessage: sera-types/src/chat.rs:19 (role: ChatRole enum, content: Option<String>) vs sera-runtime/src/types.rs:34 (role: String, camelCase, Default). Shape drift. sera-types is canonical per dep-graph. sera-runtime callers should switch.

Note: D10 (TranscriptEntry) is already tracked as sera-bb39 — not reopened here.

title: [cleanup] Duplicate trait Tool — sera-tools::registry vs sera-types::tool
description:
From dup audit 2026-04-23 (evening). trait Tool defined twice with incompatible surfaces:
- rust/crates/sera-tools/src/registry.rs:7 — minimal {name, description} for a lookup registry
- rust/crates/sera-types/src/tool.rs:612 — full async {metadata, schema, execute(input, ctx) -> Result<ToolOutput, ToolError>, risk_level}

These are not the same contract. The sera-tools registry Tool is a cataloguing shim; the sera-types Tool is the real dispatchable abstraction. Having both named Tool causes import ambiguity and makes it easy to implement the wrong one. Plan: rename registry::Tool → ToolDescriptor (or drop it entirely if the sera-types variant can do catalogue too).

title: [cleanup] GenerationMarker + BuildIdentity duplicated across telemetry/gateway/types
description:
From dup audit 2026-04-23 (evening). Two pairs of types for build/generation identity:
- GenerationMarker: sera-gateway/src/envelope.rs:31 (flat strings: label, binary_identity: String) vs sera-telemetry/src/generation.rs:27 (typed: label: GenerationLabel, binary_identity: BuildIdentity)
- BuildIdentity: sera-telemetry/src/generation.rs:12 (version, commit, build_time: OffsetDateTime, signer_fingerprint, constitution_hash) vs sera-types/src/versioning.rs:5 (version, commit: [u8;20], build_time: chrono::DateTime, signer_fingerprint, constitution_hash)

Drift: commit is String vs [u8;20]; build_time is time::OffsetDateTime vs chrono::DateTime. Plan: pick one (sera-types::versioning::BuildIdentity is canonical per SPEC-versioning §4.6), delete the sera-telemetry copy, reconcile gateway::envelope::GenerationMarker to use BuildIdentity instead of flat strings.

title: [cleanup] Two ContentBlock enums — sera-session::transcript vs sera-types::content_block

From dup audit 2026-04-23 (evening). ContentBlock enum defined twice with drift:

- rust/crates/sera-types/src/content_block.rs:35 — 3 variants: Text/ToolUse/ToolResult{tool_name,output,error}

title: [cleanup] EvolveTokenSigner + EvolveTokenError exist twice (gateway vs auth)

title: [cleanup] Two ModelError + ModelResponse + FinishReason in sera-types vs sera-models

From dup audit 2026-04-23 (evening). sera-models crate duplicates ModelResponse, ModelError, FinishReason that already exist in sera-types::model.
- ModelResponse: sera-types/src/model.rs:107 (content?, tool_calls: Vec<ToolCall>, usage: TokenUsage, model, finish_reason) vs sera-models/src/response.rs:7 (content: String, finish_reason, usage, tool_calls?)

Real shape drift — one uses Option<String>, the other required String. Plan: sera-models should depend on sera-types and re-use the canonical types; the sera-models copies are leftovers from when sera-models was intended to be leaf-independent.

title: [cleanup] Two Event types — envelope Event/EventMsg vs gateway Event
description:
From dup audit 2026-04-23 (evening). Two incompatible 'Event' structs both in sera-types:
- rust/crates/sera-types/src/envelope.rs:111 — {id, submission_id, msg: EventMsg, trace, timestamp, parent_session_key?} (NDJSON runtime↔gateway wire, SPEC-envelope)
- rust/crates/sera-types/src/event.rs:82 — {id, kind, source, agent_id, session_key, principal, text?, recipient?, idempotency_key?, requires_approval?, timestamp, metadata} (gateway inbound event, pre-submission)

Not the same thing semantically but sharing the name Event across the same crate causes  ambiguity. Plan: rename gateway-ingress one to something like IncomingEvent or GatewayEvent, or move it to sera-gateway if it's not consumed by other crates.

title: [cleanup] Two Event/LaneQueue/QueuedEvent/QueueMode in sera-queue vs sera-db
description:
From dup audit 2026-04-23 (evening). Full duplicate stack between sera-queue and sera-db:
- LaneQueue: sera-queue/src/lane.rs:40 (steer/interrupt semantics) vs sera-db/src/lane_queue.rs:117 (global concurrency cap + shared-store)
- QueuedEvent: sera-queue/src/lane.rs:23 ({id,lane,payload,enqueued_at,mode}) vs sera-db/src/lane_queue.rs:53 ({event: Event, enqueued_at: Instant, is_steer})
- QueueMode: three copies (sera-queue, sera-db, sera-gateway::envelope:61) — variants identical but serde attrs differ (snake_case vs default)

Per rust/CLAUDE.md, sera-queue is listed as the official 'QueueBackend trait, LocalQueueBackend, GlobalThrottle' owner. The sera-db copy looks like it belongs to the DB-backed QueueBackend impl that was never migrated. Plan: sera-queue is canonical, sera-db should depend on sera-queue for these types, delete the db-local copies. gateway::envelope::QueueMode should re-export from sera-queue.

title: [cleanup] Two SessionStateMachine + SessionState enum variants drift
description:
From dup audit 2026-04-23 (evening).

SessionState enum duplicated with divergent variants:
- rust/crates/sera-session/src/state.rs:9 — {Created, Active, Idle, Suspended, Compacting, Closed} (6 variants, snake_case)
- rust/crates/sera-types/src/session.rs:28 — {Created, Active, WaitingForApproval, Compacting, Suspended, Archived, Destroyed, Spawning, TrustRequired, ReadyForPrompt, Shadow, Paused} (12+ variants, lowercase)

title: sera-gateway: differentiate Op variants for non-UserTurn wrapped routes (follow-up to sera-r1g8)
description:
sera-r1g8 wrapped tasks, permission-requests, intercom routes using Op::UserTurn — the only Op variant that existed. This is semantically wrong for replay: a task result arriving looks identical to a user message in the audit stream.

Scope: define dedicated Op variants (candidate set: Op::Task, Op::TaskResult, Op::PermissionRequest, Op::AgentDm, Op::IntercomPublish) and re-wrap the routes accordingly. Update replay tooling + docs.

Out of scope for sera-r1g8 — the envelope wrapping pattern is what was asked for, the Op taxonomy gap is a distinct concern. Document in SPEC-gateway (if not already).

Blocked by: sera-r1g8 merging.
notes:
2026-04-24 investigation finding (session): the bead's premise is inaccurate.

Scope audit (current main @ b85fab58 + Wave 3 merges landing):

- `grep -rn "Op::UserTurn" rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/` yields exactly one
  production emit site: bin/sera.rs:959 (the chat handler). The other two
  matches are a display-name match arm (session_store.rs:249) and a test
  fixture (session_store.rs:552).
- `append_envelope` has one production caller: the chat handler at
  bin/sera.rs:978.
- `rust/crates/sera-gateway/src/routes/` contains only a2a.rs, plugins.rs,
  agui.rs — there are no dedicated handlers for tasks, permission-requests,
  intercom publish, or agent DM.

So no route is currently wrapping a TaskResult/PermissionRequest/Intercom/
AgentDm as Op::UserTurn. Those routes don't emit submission envelopes at
all. The "semantic replay-replay compat issue" the bead describes does not
exist on current main.

Three paths considered:

1. Literal scope (add 4 Op variants with no callers): violates CLAUDE.md
   §2 "No features beyond what was asked. No abstractions for single-use
   code." Would introduce dead variants.
2. True scope (build 4 new route handlers + envelope emission + variants):
   scope expansion from a P3 taxonomy refactor into a feature epic.
3. Just-in-time: when a future PR actually needs to emit e.g. a TaskResult
   (because someone is wiring task-completion into the gateway), they add
   Op::TaskResult AND the emit site in the same PR. Follows the pattern
   we use elsewhere — types appear when they have a real caller.

Recommendation: close sera-qrsh as "based on incorrect premise" and let
each of the 4 candidate variants land alongside its first real emitter.
File smaller beads when the matching feature work is actually scoped.

title: sera-config core_config_requires_database_url is env-racy
description:
core_config_requires_database_url at rust/crates/sera-config/src/core_config.rs:241 mutates DATABASE_URL via env::remove_var without acquiring the SERA_ENV_LOCK Mutex defined at the top of the tests module (line 238). Sister test core_config_defaults has the same problem. Any other test in the same test binary that runs concurrently and touches DATABASE_URL causes this to flake.

Observed flake on PR #985 (sera-ze27) validate-rust CI on 2026-04-20, while the same commit + test passes locally in isolation. #983 and #984 on the same origin/main base passed green — classic env-race.

Fix: wrap the two affected tests' env mutations in 'let _g = SERA_ENV_LOCK.lock().unwrap();' same as any other env-mutating test pattern. Alternatively, serialize the whole sera-config test binary via '--test-threads=1' in a test-profile setting if the pattern is pervasive.

title: sera-ze27 follow-ups: SPEC-context-engine-pluggability §4 mapping gap + object-safety test + metadata round-trip test
description:
Code-review follow-ups from sera-ze27 (PR #985). Non-blocking polish.

1. docs/plan/specs/SPEC-context-engine-pluggability.md §4 — LCM's agent-facing tool surface includes 'lcm_expand_query' (see /home/entity/.hermes/hermes-agent/plugins/context_engine/lcm/schemas.py:141). §1 and §7 name the tool but §4's mapping table has no row for it. Either add a row mapping it to 'search + expand_node + LLM synthesis' (it's a composition, not a trait method), or add an explicit non-goal note that it belongs to the sera-tool plumbing layer. §7 already argues 'tool authorship is engine-independent'; a one-sentence callout in §4 tying it to §7 closes the loop.

2. §3 one-sentence amendment — pin the reasoning for 'three traits vs one-with-defaults'. Defaults INSIDE ContextQuery are fine because any backend implementing ContextQuery at all has semantic reason to make the core four methods work. Defaults for all seven methods would force a ring-buffer engine to implement operations it has no semantic home for. Without this sentence a future reviewer may propose collapsing ContextQuery/ContextDiagnostics back into ContextEngine with defaults — the pattern used on describe_ref/expand_ref looks similar on the surface.

3. rust/crates/sera-runtime/src/context_engine/mod.rs pluggability_tests — add two tests:
   - object-safety smoke: 'let _: Arc<dyn ContextQuery> = Arc::new(NodeOnlyQuery);' catches any future async_trait break on trait-object use.
   - metadata round-trip: serialize+deserialize a ContextSearchHit or ContextSubtreeDescription with a non-empty metadata: serde_json::Value so the #[serde(default)] forward-compat slot is locked in.

4. (Deferred decision) ContextError::Unsupported variant — code reviewer flagged that defaults on describe_ref/expand_ref use Internal, which is semantically a capability error not an internal fault. Keeping Internal matches hindsight's SemanticError::Backend pattern (sera-memory) for consistency. If the LCM adapter bead finds this painful (callers need to string-sniff), add Unsupported(String) to both SemanticError and ContextError in one shot.

title: sera-memory code-review follow-ups: sqlite scope columns + default features + in_memory insert_entry visibility
description:
Non-blocking follow-ups from sera-50y1 code review:
1. rust/crates/sera-memory/src/sqlite_store.rs:443 — SqliteMemoryStore does not persist scope_kind/scope_key columns, so rows returned from query() always have scope=None. Breaks the precision of query_hierarchical when sqlite is the backend with multiple scopes. Either add the columns (match pgvector GH#140 schema) or document the limitation in the module header.
2. rust/crates/sera-memory/Cargo.toml:7 — default = ['sqlite', 'sqlite-vec']. Consider default = [] so downstream consumers that disable-default-features don't silently pay attention to defaults they didn't ask for.
3. rust/crates/sera-memory/src/in_memory.rs:125 — insert_entry is pub on a testing-only helper but reachable from production code that depends on sera-testing. Mark #[doc(hidden)] or rename __test_insert_entry.
4. Run 'cargo update --workspace' to confirm no lockfile drift from the pgvector dep move (Cargo.lock diff was zero in the extract PR — unusual but not incorrect).

- TerminationCondition enum: MaxMessages(u32), TextMention(String), Timeout(Duration), AgentDecision, ExternalSignal
- Composition: TerminationCondition::And(Box<TC>, Box<TC>), TerminationCondition::Or(Box<TC>, Box<TC>)
- Default when unset: MaxMessages(50) | Timeout(30min)
- CircleBlackboard struct with append-only VecDeque<BlackboardEntry>, retention/compaction policy
- BlackboardEntry: participant_id, timestamp, artifact_type, payload (Value)
- Blackboard read API: entries_since(cursor), entries_by_participant, snapshot()
- When termination triggers: stop message sent, circle session archived

- CircleBlackboard accessible to all policy branches in Coordinator::run

title: [GH#140] Hierarchical memory scopes: agent → circle → org traversal
description:
Decomposes sera-0tu. Implement scope hierarchy for SemanticMemoryStore queries so memory lookups can walk agent→circle→org inheritance. Current semantic_memory queries are agent_id-scoped only.

Files:
- sera-types/src/semantic_memory.rs (add Scope enum + ScopeHierarchy)
- sera-db/src/pgvector_store.rs (Scope-aware query path, UNION of scope levels)
- sera-testing semantic store mirror
- sera-runtime/src/context_engine/enricher.rs (consult hierarchy ordering)

Design:
- Scope: Agent(id) < Circle(id) < Org(id) < Global
- query(scope, k, filters) returns merged top-k across levels, with per-level score dampening (1.0 / 0.7 / 0.5 / 0.3 defaults)
- Agent-local hits keep priority even if same cosine; ties broken by recency
- Config flag runtime.hierarchical_scopes_enabled (default=false)

Acceptance:
- ScopeHierarchy type in sera-types + unit tests
- pgvector store SELECT …WHERE scope_key IN (…) with damped scoring
- InMemorySemanticStore mirrors the same behaviour
- Integration test: store 3 entries (one per scope) → agent-scope query returns all 3 with agent > circle > org ordering
- cargo test --workspace green; ~10 new tests

Depends on sera-dmpl (closed). Effort: ~2 days. Part of sera-0tu GH#140.
close_reason: subsumed by sera-fee4 (commit f385fbdc) which landed pgvector + InMemorySemanticStore scope filtering + enricher wire-up using the Scope/ScopeHierarchy/MemoryHit types from 4a5c5959

title: sera-mail: implement MailCorrelator (Design B + nonce) for Mail gate ingress
description:
Implements the correlation layer that maps inbound email replies to the existing AwaitType::Mail gate. Scheduler side (MailLookup, MailThreadId, MailEvent, is_mail_ready) is already complete — this bead adds the ingress/correlator that gives thread_event() something to return.

Design: Option B (thread-id via RFC 5322 In-Reply-To/References headers) with a SERA-issued gate nonce as a fallback for clients that strip headers. Explicitly rejects Option A (sender+subject pattern matching) as spoofable and inconsistent with the threat model of neighbouring Change/Human gates.

Scope:
- New crate: sera-mail (30th workspace member)
- OutboundEnvelope type + issuance hook
- InboundMessage parser (rfc5322 via mailparse or similar)
- MailCorrelator trait with B1 (headers) → B2 (body/reply-to token) → B3 (drop)
- MailCorrelationError enum
- InMemoryMailLookup implementing sera-workflow::MailLookup
- Remove TODO(post-MVS) comment at sera-workflow/src/task.rs:230-232
- Gateway wire-up to instantiate MailCorrelator and feed events into the lookup

Out of scope:
- Persistent (Postgres) backing for MailLookup (follow-up)
- SMTP transport (existing sera-tools egress plane)
- Pattern-matching fallback (explicitly rejected)

Acceptance:
- sera-mail compiles + clippy -D warnings clean
- MailCorrelator resolves B1/B2/B2-body, drops B3
- >=5 correlator unit tests covering Gmail/Outlook web/forward/spoof/stripped-headers
- InMemoryMailLookup passes the existing 7 sera-workflow mail gate tests unchanged
- End-to-end test drives mail gate from issuance -> reply ingestion -> ready-queue
- TODO(post-MVS) comment at task.rs:230-232 removed

title: Research: Standardize skill framework on AgentSkills spec + MCP context gating
description:
Research and design task to align SERA's skill system with the AgentSkills open standard (agentskills.io).

## Background
AgentSkills is an open standard (originally by Anthropic) for portable agent skills. Adopted by Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, VS Code, OpenHands, Junie, and 30+ tools. Format: SKILL.md files with frontmatter + instructions.

SERA currently has its own skill format (gray-matter frontmatter .md files in skills/builtin/). This research explores aligning with the standard for interoperability.

## Research areas

### 1. SKILL.md format alignment
- Compare SERA's current SkillFrontMatterSchema (core/src/skills/schema.ts) with the AgentSkills spec
- What fields need mapping? What's missing?
- Can we support both formats during migration?

### 2. Skill packaging and distribution
- AgentSkills uses folders with SKILL.md + resources (scripts, templates)
- SERA's ClawHub concept (GH#329) for community skill distribution
- OCI-based distribution vs git-based vs npm-based
- How do skills reference and bundle MCP server configs?

### 3. MCP context gating via skills
- Key idea: always gate MCP tool access behind skills to protect context
- Instead of exposing raw MCP tools to the LLM, wrap them in skills that provide context + instructions
- This reduces context bloat (skill loaded on demand vs all MCP tools always visible)
- Skill defines: when to activate, what MCP tools to use, what instructions to follow
- Example: a 'database-query' skill wraps the postgres MCP server with schema context

### 4. Skill discovery and auto-activation
- AgentSkills supports trigger-based activation (keyword matching, file pattern matching)
- SERA already has trigger matching in SkillInjector (core/src/skills/SkillInjector.ts)
- How to improve: semantic matching, context-aware activation, user intent classification

### 5. Interoperability
- Can SERA consume skills written for Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini CLI?
- Can SERA publish skills that work in those tools?
- What's the minimum viable interop?

## References
- AgentSkills spec: https://agentskills.io/specification
- Example skills: https://github.com/anthropics/skills
- Reference library: https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/tree/main/skills-ref
- SERA skill schema: core/src/skills/schema.ts
- SERA skill library: core/src/skills/SkillLibrary.ts
- SERA skill injector: core/src/skills/SkillInjector.ts
- Related: GH#329 (ClawHub), GH#511 (SKILL.md format)

title: Dynamic model & provider routing with health-aware selection
description:
Research & design for intelligent, dynamic LLM model/provider routing that adapts over time.

## Problem
Currently model selection is static — agents use a fixed model name from their manifest. When a provider is rate-limited, at capacity, or hitting limits, the only fallback is the new failoverModels chain (#860). There's no intelligence about which model to pick based on real-time conditions.

## Vision
A dynamic routing layer that:

1. **Auto-discovers available models** from connected providers (LM Studio, OpenRouter, Google AI Studio, etc.) and keeps the model catalog fresh via periodic polling
2. **Health-aware selection** — tracks per-model/provider metrics:
   - Request success rate, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
   - Rate limit status (429 counts, retry-after headers)
   - Capacity signals (queue depth, concurrent request count)
   - Tool call success rate per model (some models are bad at tool use)
   - Cost per token (for budget-aware routing)
3. **Smart routing policies**:
   - Round-robin with health weighting
   - Cost-optimized (prefer cheapest healthy model)
   - Quality-optimized (prefer model with best tool success rate)
   - Latency-optimized (prefer fastest healthy model)
   - Agent-specific preferences (e.g., "sera uses reasoning models, helper uses fast models")
4. **Statistics & learning** — accumulate per-model stats over time:
   - Tool call failure rates by model (some models hallucinate tool args)
   - Response quality signals (if available from downstream feedback)
   - Time-of-day patterns (some providers are slower at peak hours)
5. **Dashboard** — expose routing decisions, model health, and stats via API + web UI

## Architecture sketch
- `ModelRouter` service in sera-core replaces/wraps current `ProviderRegistry.resolve()`
- `ModelHealthTracker` — in-memory + periodic DB flush of per-model metrics
- `ModelDiscoveryService` — polls connected providers for available models
- `RoutingPolicy` interface — pluggable strategies
- Stats table: `model_routing_stats` (model, window, success_count, fail_count, avg_latency_ms, tool_fail_count, ...)

## Not in scope (yet)
- Automatic model fine-tuning or prompt adaptation per model
- Cross-instance routing (multi-sera federation)

## References
- Current failover: PR #860 (failoverModels chain)
- Current circuit breaker: CircuitBreakerService.ts
- Current provider registry: ProviderRegistry.ts
- Dynamic provider discovery: DynamicProviderManager (LM Studio polling)
